papers.title: Spatially resolved tumor-microenvironment architecture defines therapeutic response in unresectable hepatoblastoma
papers.abstract: Background Hepatoblastoma exhibits variable therapeutic response that is not fully explained by current risk stratification. While prior studies have characterized tumor composition, the role of spatial organization in determining outcome, particularly in unresectable disease requiring transplantation under immunosuppression, remains unclear. Methods We integrated spatial transcriptomics using the 10x Genomics Visium platform ( n = 11 tumors) with single-cell spatial molecular imaging using NanoString CosMx ( n = 3 tumors) on post-chemotherapy explant specimens across clinically defined groups (relapse-prone unresectable, non-relapse unresectable, and resectable hepatoblastoma). Spatial deconvolution, module scoring, spatial co-localization, and cell-cell interaction analyses were used to define region-level transcriptional programs and their underlying cellular organization. Results We identified three spatial architectures associated with clinical outcome. Relapse-prone tumors exhibited a centralized, TME-dominated organization enriched for progenitor-like, cycling, and stress-responsive tumor cell states co-localized with SPP1+ TAMs and CAFs, with enrichment of hypoxia response, extracellular matrix remodeling, and Midkine (MDK-LRP1) signaling. Non-relapse tumors displayed a distributed architecture with compartmentalized tumor-immune interactions, increased immune engagement, and preserved epithelial differentiation, including inflammatory hepatocyte-like states. Resection samples showed reduced tumor cell state heterogeneity and more uniform TME-immune organization. Conclusions: Integration of regional and single-cell spatial transcriptomics across two platforms reveals that the chemo-remodeled tumor architecture of hepatoblastoma encodes spatially organized tumor cell-TME interactions as central determinants of therapeutic response. Translational Relevance Current risk stratification in hepatoblastoma — principally based on staging and clinical features — does not reliably predict therapeutic response, particularly in unresectable disease. Our findings identify that spatial tumor-microenvironment (TME) organization is a key determinant of patient outcome. Specifically, our analysis reveals that disease relapse is driven by specialized macrophage-fibroblast signaling networks that promote an immune-cold, therapy-resistant niche. We define a spatially derived gene signature capturing this high-risk TME, which demonstrates strong prognostic value across independent cohorts, highlighting its potential utility as a biomarker for refined patient stratification. These results strongly suggest that incorporating spatial biomarkers into clinical assessment can improve the choice of therapy. Furthermore, the identification of Midkine (MDK) signaling and macrophage-stromal crosstalk as key components of relapse-associated architecture provides a direct rationale for targeting TME communication to combat therapeutic resistance. Together, this work supports a crucial shift from composition-based to spatially informed approaches for risk assessment and therapeutic targeting in hepatoblastoma.

papers.title: Targeting a Calcium-Associated Mitochondrial Vulnerability in TET2-Deficient Myeloid Cells.
papers.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) driven by loss-of-function mutations in TET2 is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, yet therapeutic strategies capable of preferentially targeting pathogenic TET2-deficient myeloid effector cells remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a TET2 loss-of-function-associated ion-mitochondrial vulnerability that enables preferential pharmacological suppression of TET2-deficient macrophages. Using chemical-genetic profiling, we find that perturbation of ion homeostasis preferentially compromises survival of TET2-deficient macrophages through increased mitochondrial-enriched Ca2+-sensitive signaling and activation of intrinsic apoptotic pathways. The cardiac glycoside Lanatoside C preferentially induces mitochondrial depolarization and apoptosis in TET2-deficient macrophages, with substantially smaller effects in control cells. In multicellular human cardiac organoids, preferential reduction of TET2-knockdown macrophages suppresses inflammatory remodeling, reduces cardiomyocyte apoptosis and fibrosis, and improves abnormal calcium-handling dynamics. In a murine partial donor-cell reconstitution model, Lanatoside C reduced relative donor-derived monocyte and neutrophil frequencies in Tet2-deficient donor-cell recipients; these findings do not establish effects on stem-cell fitness. Together, these findings identify a pharmacologically exploitable ion-mitochondrial vulnerability associated with TET2 loss-of-function and establish human cardiac organoids as a platform for causal interrogation of immune-driven cardiovascular pathology.

papers.title: Periodontal Phenotype Modification of Mandibular Incisors Following Augmented Corticotomy During Orthodontic-Orthognathic Treatment in Skeletal Class III Patients: A Long-Term Prospective Cohort Study.

papers.title: Comparative Transcriptomic Signatures of Keloids and Hypertrophic Scars: A Genetic Association Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundKeloids and hypertrophic scars are fibroproliferative skin disorders with overlapping clinical features but distinct biological behaviors, posing major therapeutic challenges in plastic and reconstructive surgery. Understanding their molecular mechanisms is critical for developing targeted interventions.MethodsA comparative study of transcriptomic profiles of keloid (n = 3) and hypertrophic scar (n = 3) lesions from female patients (thoracic region, no comorbidities). RNA-seq was performed, and differential gene expression was analyzed using DESeq2. Functional enrichment analyses were conducted via Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, stratifying upregulated and downregulated genes.ResultsKeloids exhibited upregulation of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis, RNA splicing, chromosomal organization, and cell cycle progression (eg, USP39, CEP85, RNF180, VHL), reflecting a sustained anabolic and proliferative state. In contrast, hypertrophic scars were enriched in immune and metabolic pathways, with higher expression of ICAM1, MRC1/CD206, PDE2A, TMEM120A, and TMEM135, suggesting modulation by inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6, transforming growth factor beta) and M2 macrophage polarization. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for translational strategies in plastic surgery, including precision-targeted therapies, drug repurposing, and gene-based interventions, advancing management of pathological skin fibrosis and improving surgical outcomes.

papers.title: Single‑cell multi‑omics analysis reveals TGF-β1-RUNX2-mediated matCAF differentiation and its role in remodeling the lymph node metastatic microenvironment in bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) in bladder cancer (BCa) is associated with poor clinical outcomes and may contribute to the development of metastatic tolerance, yet the stromal mechanisms underlying this process remain incompletely understood. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, clinical cohorts, and functional models, we identified an LNM-enriched matrix-remodeling cancer-associated fibroblast (matCAF) state characterized by LRRC15 and POSTN expression and associated with adverse survival and reduced immunotherapy response. Mechanistically, Hybrid_CCND1⁺ malignant epithelial cells promoted matCAF differentiation through FOS-dependent TGFB1 transcription and TGF-β1-TGFBR1-RUNX2 signaling. Spatial analyses further revealed barrier-like accumulation of matCAFs at tumor-stroma interfaces and linked matCAF-rich neighborhoods to enhanced PI3K activity and lymphangiogenesis-related programs. Functionally, matCAF-derived POSTN engaged ITGAV/ITGB5 to activate PI3K-AKT signaling and promote tumor and lymphatic endothelial remodeling. MatCAFs were also associated with SPP1⁺ macrophage remodeling and impaired CD8⁺ T-cell function, partly through RUNX2-associated CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling. Pharmacological disruption of the RUNX2-dependent matCAF program reduced tumor burden and partially restored T-cell activity in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify matCAF-centered stromal remodeling as a potential cellular basis of the metastatic-tolerance niche in BCa LNM and provide proof-of-concept for therapeutic targeting of the matCAF program.

papers.title: NLRP3 signalling in NSCLC: distinguishing expression, inflammasome activation and context-dependent function.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality despite advances in targeted therapy and immune checkpoint blockade. NLRP3-associated inflammation has attracted increasing interest in NSCLC, yet interpretation of the available evidence remains challenging because molecular expression, inflammasome activation, cytokine processing, pyroptotic execution and pathway dependence are frequently considered together. Here, we present a structured narrative review and an evidence framework that separates the biological event directly measured from the level of NLRP3-specific mechanistic support, while independently considering cellular source, disease relevance and treatment context. Current evidence indicates that NLRP3-specific mechanistic dependence in NSCLC has been demonstrated only in selected experimental settings, particularly treatment-conditioned macrophage models. Treatment-naïve human evidence reveals compartment-specific inflammasome-associated responses in alveolar macrophages and peripheral leukocytes but does not establish NLRP3 dependence. Tumour-cell studies support treatment-induced inflammasome- and pyroptosis-associated phenotypes, although causal attribution to NLRP3 is often incomplete. Single-cell and spatial studies mainly identify NLRP3-related transcriptional states or candidate microenvironmental niches and cannot, by themselves, demonstrate functional inflammasome activation or NLRP3-dependent interactions. Clinical trials targeting IL-1β provide evidence for downstream inflammatory modulation but do not directly evaluate NLRP3 inhibition. Overall, current evidence supports context-dependent NLRP3-associated biology in NSCLC rather than a uniform biomarker or therapeutic target. Future studies integrating cell-resolved localisation, activation-specific measurements, pathway perturbation and longitudinal validation are required to determine whether clinically relevant NLRP3-dependent states can be reproducibly identified.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal transcriptomic signatures of resident cardiac macrophages and macrophage-associated spatial states during acute myocardial infarction.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAcute myocardial infarction (AMI) followed by reperfusion result in a phasic response by cardiac macrophages. During the first 7 days after AMI, macrophage populations exhibit dynamic phenotypic changes. Ultimately, inflammatory damage results in ventricular remodeling and fibrosis. Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) were isolated using flow cytometry and analyzed with NanoString. Pathway enrichment analysis annotated statistically significant genes. We employed transcriptome-wide, spatiotemporal analysis of cardiac tissue samples during AMI.ResultsNanoString analysis of pooled RCM samples identified candidate differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between time points, and pathway enrichment analysis suggested inflammatory, reparative, and extracellular matrix-associated programs during early AMI. Visium spatial transcriptomic analysis of cardiac tissue samples identified spatial patterns consistent with six macrophage-associated transcriptional states within the cardiac compartment. Integration of NanoString, Visium, and immunostaining data revealed temporal and spatial patterns of S100a9-associated macrophage signatures during early AMI. We also observed spatial co-localization of macrophage-associated and fibrosis-associated transcripts in injured regions.ConclusionsThese findings provide insight into cardiac macrophage-associated transcriptional programs during AMI and identify candidate inflammatory, reparative, and fibrosis-associated pathways for future mechanistic investigation.

papers.title: RUNX1-Mediated Hypoxic Signaling Impairs Myogenesis and Promotes Fibrosis in Myopathies.
papers.abstract: Compromised myogenic repair with enhanced fibrosis is common in myopathies, including Wooden Breast (WB) myopathy in broilers, but the underlying mechanism of their co-occurrence remains elusive. Using WB myopathy as a model, we investigated the common pathological origins of these co-occurring features. Our single-nucleus RNA sequencing results showed enhanced oxidative stress and profibrotic remodeling of myofibers, increased proliferation but decreased differentiation of satellite cells (SCs), and aggravated differentiation of fibroblasts (FBs) in WB samples. Differential gene expression and pseudotime trajectory analysis further identified RUNX1 as a key regulator for both SCs and FBs, which was further supported by gene functional studies in respective cell culture models. Moreover, reduced blood flow and oxygen supply may indicate a hypoxic state in WB muscle, which was associated with enhanced RUNX1 expression. Consistently, coordinately enhanced HIF1A and RUNX1 expressions were found in differentiated FBs of human muscles and in muscles with diseases. Collectively, our study found that hypoxia-associated upregulation of RUNX1 disrupted the myogenic progression of SCs and exacerbated fibrotic differentiation of FBs, contributing to pathological degeneration in myopathies. Targeting RUNX1 may therefore represent a potential therapeutic strategy for prevention and treatment, which warrants future in vivo investigations.

papers.title: Integrated Multiomic Analysis Reveals an EBV-Associated MIF-SPP1+ Macrophage Axis Linking Tumor Stemness and Immune Dysfunction in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Elucidating how Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) shapes tumor-immune interactions is important for improving therapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Collectively, these findings support an EBV-associated MIF-SPP1 macrophage-tumor/T-cell crosstalk model linking stemness-associated epithelial phenotypes with immune dysfunction and adverse clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Polymeric Biomaterials with Multiple Stratified Layers for Periodontal Ligament/Bone Regeneration: A Review.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic pathological condition initiated by bacterial plaque accumulation and characterized by the progressive destruction of the tooth-supporting tissues, including the periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone. If left untreated, it may result in tooth mobility, pathologic tooth migration, and ultimately tooth loss. Despite numerous regenerative strategies, complete periodontal regeneration remains challenging. Guided tissue regeneration (GTR) and guided bone regeneration (GBR) promote the regeneration of the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone; however, current GTR/GBR biomaterials often exhibit inadequate mechanical stability and osseointegration. To overcome these limitations, various multilayer biomaterials with enhanced functionalities have been developed. This review outlines the key properties required for GTR/GBR, evaluates the design and performance of current multilayer biomaterials, and examines their major limitations, particularly their inability to fully replicate native periodontal tissues due to structural incompatibilities between layers. Finally, future directions and recommendations are presented to guide the development of next-generation GTR/GBR biomaterials.

papers.title: Decoding molecular heterogeneity in lupus nephritis: integrating single-cell and spatial multi-omics for endotype-driven precision therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) develops in 40-60% of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and remains the leading cause of renal morbidity and progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). While the upstream immunological events initiating LN-including loss of self-tolerance, pathogenic autoantibody production, glomerular immune complex deposition, and type I interferon (IFN) activation-are broadly shared, accumulating evidence demonstrates that these convergent triggers give rise to molecularly heterogeneous tissue injury programs at the renal level. This fundamental divergence provides a mechanistic explanation for the inconsistent therapeutic responses observed with standardized immunosuppressive protocols. Advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial gene expression mapping, CITE-seq, and cross-platform multi-omic integration have deconvolved this heterogeneity into at least five recognizable tissue-level injury programs: (i) an IFN-γ-polarized macrophage-tubular epithelial cell co-activation circuit, (ii) a Tfh-B cell ectopic germinal center pathway, (iii) a neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-driven inflammatory cascade, (iv) a podocyte-autonomous injury program, and (v) a TREM2+ macrophage-orchestrated fibrotic program. Concurrently, multiplexed urinary biomarker platforms are under development as non-invasive surrogates for tissue-level pathogenic activity. This review synthesizes current understanding of disease mechanisms, molecular profiling evidence, biomarker candidates, and mechanism-directed therapies corresponding to each tissue injury program. We map existing and investigational agents-including anifrolumab, obinutuzumab, voclosporin, CAR-T cell therapy, and complement inhibitors-to their mechanistic targets and delineate the design requirements for prospective biomarker-stratified trials essential to validating molecularly guided treatment selection.

papers.title: SpaAxFormer: Fine-Grained Token Modeling of Spatial Transcriptomics with Axial Transformers
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics combines gene-expression measurements with spatial relationships between cells. We investigate how spatial context can be incorporated into gene-resolved representations while preserving explicit input-gene correspondence. SpaAxFormer is a spatially constrained factorized formulation that maintains contextual cell-gene states throughout the encoder. It first contextualizes genes within each cell and then exchanges corresponding gene states across spatial neighbors, while a separate CLS representation provides a cell-level summary. Contextual gene states support gene-expression reconstruction, while CLS-conditioned reconstruction and contrastive learning provide complementary supervision for the cell-level representation. We evaluate SpaAxFormer on gene-expression imputation and spatial-domain identification across multiple spatial-transcriptomics technologies. Compared with the included baselines, imputation results were most favorable on dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) datasets and more mixed on additional technologies, while post-hoc spatial refinement consistently improved mean ARI on the Visium spatial-domain datasets where it was applied. In a single-slice component-addition analysis, mean clustering ARI increased as CLS-conditioned reconstruction and contrastive supervision were added. Together, these results show that the same gene-resolved formulation can support complementary gene-level prediction and cell-level spatial representation while preserving explicit input-gene correspondence.

papers.title: Single Nucleus Profiling Reveals Rewired Tumor-Immune-Stromal Cell Communication in Plasmacytoid Urothelial Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Plasmacytoid urothelial carcinoma (PUC) is an aggressive histologic subtype of bladder cancer associated with worse patient outcomes and therapeutic response compared to conventional urothelial carcinoma (CUC). Taken together, this study delineates PUC architecture and demonstrates interplay CDH1-low tumor cells, EMT, and immunosuppressive macrophages, identifying possible therapeutic vulnerabilities in PUC.

papers.title: Statistical significance testing for spatial domain detection in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: In spatial transcriptomics, domain-detection methods group platform-specific spatial measurement units—cells, bins or multicellular spots—into spatial domains for comparing molecular programs, cellular composition and interactions among tissue regions. However, the number of candidate domains detected in the same tissue can vary with user-specified parameters or model-selection criteria. Whether candidate domains should be merged can be framed as a test of a single-domain null hypothesis, under which each gene has constant mean expression across all spatial units in the combined region. However, testing candidate domains on the same gene-expression data used to detect them may induce post-selection bias and yield anti-conservative p-values, increasing the risk of oversegmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce SigDoTS (statistical Significance testing for Domain deTection in Spatial transcriptomics), a hypothesis-testing framework for spatial domain detection. SigDoTS uses hierarchical testing to determine which candidate domains to retain or merge, with adjustment for family-wise error control. It accounts for gene–gene covariance and spatial dependence and computes p-values by rerunning the upstream domain-detection pipeline on datasets simulated under the fitted single-domain null. In simulations, SigDoTS controlled the type I error rate at the root node under the single-domain null and improved recovery of the true spatial domains when multiple domains were present. In human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, SigDoTS retained superficial and deep Layer 6 domains but merged Layer 3 candidate domains across different initial numbers of candidate domains. In ovarian and colorectal cancers, SigDoTS retained epithelial domains with different gene-expression programs and local immune environments, together with immune, stromal and vascular domains.

papers.title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients
papers.abstract: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal study, where we collected comprehensive clinical data over a one-year period on each patient in the process of changing their therapy. Methods: Samples from minimally invasive, ultrasound‐guided synovial biopsies were collected from RA patients at baseline prior to start of a new therapy and 4-6‐week follow‐up under IRB-approved protocols with informed consent. Comprehensive clinical data from each appointment were recorded into a shared REDCap database. Failure to respond to therapy was based on clinical disease activity index (CDAI) for RA after 12-18 weeks post therapy. Biopsied samples were dissociated, enriched for CD45⁺ or CD45⁺CD11b⁺ cells, and processed on the 10X Genomics Chromium platform to generate libraries for single-cell RNA sequencing with cell-surface protein detection (CITE-seq). Spatial transcriptomics were performed on formalin-fixed paraffin embedded sections analyzed with 10X Xenium and NanoString CosMx. Results: We performed CITE-seq analysis on ~38,000 CD45+ synovial cells isolated from 17 patients who failed a conventional or biologic DMARD and planned to change therapy. We then subclustered on the myeloid population to reveal 12 myeloid subpopulations that consist of macrophages (n = 8), Osteoclast-like cells, DCs (n = 2) and proliferating cells. The proportion of cDCs was significantly higher in responders, while the proportion of macrophages was significantly lower in responders. The proportion of ISG15+ and THBS1+macrophages were enriched in the non-responder patients. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that ISG15+ macrophages were preferentially localized to the synovial lining, while the THBS1+ macrophages are likely interacting with lymphoid cells within the sublining tissue. Conclusions: These data are among the first to prospectively profile macrophage populations as predictors of response to therapy. Future studies are required to verify whether myeloid subpopulation associations hold across specific therapies.

papers.title: B cells dominate the heart immune infiltrate during chronic infectious cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell and spatially resolved multi-omics have revolutionised our understanding of the cellular and molecular niches governing cardiac homeostasis and acute injury. However, the immune-stromal networks sustaining long-term, chronic heart pathology remain poorly defined, largely due to a paucity of physiologically relevant experimental models. CellChat intercellular communication modelling identifies plasma cell-fibroblast crosstalk as the strongest immune-stromal interaction in the fibrosis-prone heart, driven by predicted matrix anchoring (CD44-collagen/laminin) and molecular survival axes (App-Cd74, C3-Cr2). Supporting these computational predictions, immunofluorescence and spatial profiling confirm close proximity between plasma B cells and fibroblasts, alongside a striking accumulation of B cells embedded within extracellular matrix-rich cardiac scars. This localised B cell response maintains prominent pools of parasite-reactive and heart-autoreactive antibody-secreting cells despite a lack of detectable parasite signal in their immediate micro-vicinity. Together, these findings identify a matrix-associated plasma B cell-fibroblast niche as a central driver of chronic cardiac remodelling, revealing how persistent tissue scarring can become decoupled from direct local pathogen presence.

papers.title: Dysregulated B Cell Education Drives Autoimmunity and Immunodeficiency in Down Syndrome
papers.abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) present with both increased rates of autoimmunity and immunodeficiency. To understand this paradox, we first examined lymph node (LN) architecture and immune cell composition in infants with and without DS, as well as peripheral blood B cells from unrelated adults with and without DS. Most strikingly, LNs from individuals with DS exhibited a marked paucity of germinal centers compared with typical lymph nodes. Stromal cells within DS LNs expressed significantly lower levels of the adhesion molecules ICAM1 and VCAM1, accompanied by significantly reduced CXCR5 expression within B cell follicles, suggesting impaired B cell migration and follicular organization. Although fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) were present at comparable frequencies in DS and control LNs, MARCO lymphatic endothelial cells (MARCO-LECs), another critical stromal cell population supporting LN architecture, were significantly reduced. In addition, follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), which are essential for antigen retention and B cell selection within germinal centers, were also substantially reduced. To determine the consequences of these abnormalities on humoral immunity, we performed paired single-cell RNA sequencing and V(D)J sequencing of peripheral blood B cells from adults with and without DS. DS memory and CD86 switched memory B cell populations exhibited significantly elevated reactive oxygen species and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling gene signatures, coupled with reduced levels of somatic hypermutation in the memory population and increase usage of the autoreactivity-associated IGHV4-34 heavy-chain gene. Collectively, these findings suggest that early-life disruption of LN architecture, characterized by reduced expression of adhesion molecules, selective loss of MARCO-LECs, and depletion of FDCs, impairs germinal center function and B cell education. This defective microenvironment likely contributes to inadequate affinity maturation, as reflected by diminished somatic hypermutation and a more autoreactive B cell repertoire in adults with Down syndrome.

papers.title: PRISM: probabilistic cell-type resolution with integrated spatial modelling for simultaneous ambient RNA decontamination and doublet correction in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics count matrices are confounded by ambient RNA contamination and cell-segmentation doublets, two artifacts that co-occur but are rarely modelled jointly. We present PRISM, an Expectation-Maximization framework that simultaneously (i) assigns each cell a probabilistic cell-type identity, (ii) detects doublets via log-likelihood ratio testing of two-component mixtures, and (iii) estimates a per-cell contamination fraction α anchored to a spatially resolved ambient profile. In an in silico benchmark of 40,800 simulated cells, PRISM recovers α with Pearson r=1.000 across all contamination levels (0.05 to 0.50) and UMI depths (500 to 5,000), with zero doublet false positives and 100% singlet accuracy. Applied to a Visium HD mouse cerebellum dataset (four samples, 125,289 cells, 17 reference types) from a metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD) model, PRISM identifies a median α=0.60, flags 67.4% doublets (driven by the densely packed cerebellar granule layer), eliminates spurious myelin signal from microglia (0.82% to 0.00%), and doubles oligodendrocyte myelin purity (2.8% to 5.6%). PRISM runs on commodity CPUs in under 15 minutes and returns decontaminated integer count matrices for every measured gene.

papers.title: DECONVersation: Single Cell Foundation Model-Derived Embeddings for Robust Cell Type Deconvolution of Bulk RNA-seq
papers.abstract: Motivation: Bulk RNA-seq deconvolution uses single-cell references to estimate cell type proportions in bulk tissue. papers.title: Dissecting human embryonic patterning during organogenesis reveals a rostral midline progenitor population for mesoendoderm induction
papers.abstract: Understanding how human organogenesis is accomplished via intricate spatiotemporal patterning of organ primordia requires spatial atlases at cellular resolution. However, existing human embryo spatial atlases are built using sequencing-based platforms such as Stereo-seq, which have limited spatial resolution and blurred anatomical boundaries, leading to misclassification across adjacent cells. Here, we integrate in situ imaging-based transcriptomics (Xenium) with transcriptome-wide spatial profiling (Visium-HD) of Carnegie stages 9-12 embryos to delineate the patterning of core embryonic tissues at single-cell resolution, including the brain, spinal cord, somites, neural crest, notochord, heart, and gut tube. A new finding enabled by spatial single-cell resolution is the identification of rostral midline progenitors (RMPs), a cell population co-expressing SOX2, TBXT, and OTX2. Transcriptionally, RMPs are distinct from both neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) and prechordal mesoderm, and in vivo clonal barcoding in mice indicates that RMPs share a common developmental origin with rostral neural ectoderm. To interrogate their functional significance, we leveraged our spatial transcriptome data to recapitulate RMP-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells and showed that these cells can induce epiblast-like cells to acquire mesendodermal and endodermal fates, while themselves adopting an ectodermal fate consistent with their in vivo counterparts. This work provides a 3D, stage-resolved molecular cell atlas of tissue patterning in human embryo that serves as a reference for in vitro models.

papers.title: THiRST: Computer Vision Empowered Three-dimensional High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Analytics

papers.title: Redefining Synovial Pathotypes in Psoriatic Arthritis through Multi-Modal Histology and Machine Learning (The PSYNOVIUM Study)
papers.abstract: BackgroundSynovial inflammation in psoriatic arthritis (PsA) lacks a validated histological classification framework. Current approaches apply rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovial pathotypes to PsA, which overlooks immunobiological differences between the diseases and limits the predictive power of tissue stratification. We aimed to define data-driven, PsA-specific synovial pathotypes to facilitate tissue-driven precision medicine. MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were obtained from 61 patients with PsA (n=22), seropositive RA (n=23), seronegative RA (n=10), and other inflammatory arthritides (n=6). Sections underwent multi-modal staining, including H&E, picrosirius red, and immunohisto-chemistry for CD3, CD20, CD68, CD138, and CD31. Whole-slide digital image analysis and automated pixel classifiers quantified cellular and stromal metrics. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering identified intrinsic PsA pathotypes, which were correlated with clinical disease activity, radiographic osteoarthritis (OA), and longitudinal treatment responses. FindingsWhile a subset of PsA patients shared an inflammatory signature with seropositive RA, unsupervised clustering of the PsA cohort revealed three distinct, novel pathotypes: Dense Myeloid (macrophage-driven), Fibro-Stromal (fibrosis and pauci-immune), and Angio-Lymphoid (hypervascular with significant CD138+ plasma cell infiltration). Pathotypes were independent of treatment and concurrent radiographic knee OA. The Fibro-Stromal pathotype correlated with significantly higher cutaneous psoriasis severity. Longitudinally, patients with the Fibro-Stromal pathotype exhibited a trend toward lower treatment response (44%) following standard interventions (methotrexate or TNF inhibitors) compared to the Dense Myeloid (50%) and Angio-Lymphoid (80%) pathotypes. InterpretationWe present the first computationally derived synovial pathotypes specific to PsA, revealing distinct plasma cell and fibrotic architectures not captured by RA-centric models. To enable clinical translation, we distilled these findings into a pragmatic, four-marker diagnostic decision tree (CD31, CD68, CD138, and picrosirius red) designed for routine histopathology workflows, providing a staging ground for biomarker-stratified clinical trials in PsA. FundingFunding from the NIHR Biomedical Research Centre: Manchester, Arthritis UK, the Wellcome Trust, Brit-PACT, the National Psoriasis Foundation, and the Medical Research Council. Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSThe potential clinical utility of tissue-based patient stratification is well established in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), where baseline synovial pathotypes (lympho-myeloid, diffuse-myeloid, and pauciimmune) have guided targeted biologic therapy in landmark precision medicine trials. However, psoriatic arthritis (PsA) exhibits a fundamentally distinct synovial microenvironment, characterised by unique vascular architecture, altered stromal fibroblast phenotypes, and distinct immune infiltrates intertwined with the IL-23/IL-17 cytokine axis. Consequently, attempting to classify PsA synovial tissue using established RA-derived scoring systems risks misrepresenting intrinsic disease biology. There is currently no validated, disease-specific histological classification system for PsA, which forces therapeutic decision-making to rely on an empirical, trial-and-error approach rather than underlying target tissue pathobiology. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first study to define data-driven, computationally derived synovial pathotypes entirely specific to PsA. By leveraging multi-modal digital pathology and unsupervised machine learning, we deconstructed the PsA synovium into three biologically distinct pathotypes: Dense Myeloid, Fibro-Stromal, and Angio-Lymphoid. We demonstrated that the highly inflammatory PsA microenvironment is distinctly driven by CD138+ plasma cells rather than the CD20+ B cells typically observed in RA. Furthermore, we identified a striking tissue-level divergence: patients with the highly fibrotic, pauci-immune Fibro-Stromal pathotype exhibited the most severe cutaneous psoriasis and demonstrated a trend toward higher failure rates on standard therapies, independent of concurrent osteoarthritis. Crucially, we translated these high-dimensional computational findings into a pragmatic, four-marker diagnostic decision tree (incorporating CD31, CD68, CD138, and picrosirius red). Implications of all the available evidenceThis study establishes that PsA synovial pathology requires a dedicated, disease-specific classification framework. The proposed diagnostic decision tree can be integrated into routine clinical histopathology workflows without the immediate need for advanced spatial or single-cell transcriptomics. Furthermore, the correlation between the Fibro-Stromal pathotype, severe skin disease, and poor joint response to standard therapies provides a biological rationale for stratifying this specific subgroup towards early IL-17 or IL-23 inhibitor intervention alongside conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. papers.title: Single-cell profiling of human plaques reveals cellular and molecular signatures of symptomatic atherosclerosis
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability drives ischemic cardiovascular events, yet the cellular and molecular signatures distinguishing symptomatic from asymptomatic human plaques remain poorly defined. Here, we compared 53 symptomatic and asymptomatic human carotid plaques using single-nucleus (snRNA-seq; 17 samples, 19,100 nuclei; AtherOMICS biobank) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; 36 samples, 68,983 cells; four public datasets), analyzed independently and combined by meta-analysis. These findings provide novel insights into cellular and molecular phenotypes associated with plaque vulnerability and identify potential driver mechanisms of symptomatic plaque transformation that could inform therapeutic development.

papers.title: DisCell: Separating Spillover from Niche Response in Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution measures every cell in its place in the tissue, but diffusion and segmentation errors also add transcripts of neighboring cells to a cell's counts. This spillover makes a cell resemble its neighbors, and a response to the niche makes cells in the same niche resemble each other. Both tie a cell's expression to its surroundings. The count data alone cannot tell the two apart. Findings from single-cell transcriptomes, such as a gene program that is higher in one niche than in another or signaling genes that change depending on the neighborhood, may therefore be artifacts of spillover. Current models describe a cell by its intrinsic state together with either its niche response or spillover, but none models all three. We present DisCell, the first method that models all three components jointly and measures how robust each finding is to spillover. DisCell is a generative model that describes single-cell gene expression profiles in terms of two latent variables, an intrinsic state and a response to the niche, and adds spillover from its neighbors as a separate term. DisCell fits the model at increasing levels of spillover and recomputes each finding on the spillover-free expression to see how much spillover it withstands. DisCell also estimates the most spillover a section can contain, and a finding that holds even at that amount is not explained by spillover. In simulated tissue, DisCell recovers each cell's intrinsic state and response and tells findings created by spillover apart from genuine responses. On five sections of ovarian and lung tissue, the intrinsic state keeps more of each cell's own properties, measured by its cell-cycle phase, than any competing method that holds as little of its neighborhood. Within each cell type, the model partitions the variation of each gene into intrinsic state, niche response and spillover. Using DisCell, we rank findings about niches by their robustness to spillover and confirm that a previously reported finding withstands spillover, that esophageal cancer cells in niches infiltrated by immune or stromal cells express more of an epithelial-mesenchymal transition program. DisCell also predicts what the gene expression of a cell type would be in another niche, with its spillover part separated, at lower error on most tasks than the competing method built for this purpose. Training the model takes under ten minutes on one consumer GPU for sections of up to 400,000 cells.

papers.title: Virtual dynamics of spatiotemporal single-cell interactions
papers.abstract: Building virtual cells and tissues requires reconstructing how interacting cell populations evolve in space and time, yet spatial omics experiments provide only sparse snapshots of this process. Here, we introduce CytoBridge, a computational method that reconstructs continuous virtual cell dynamics from discrete spatial transcriptomic data. papers.title: Regionalisation of muscle nucleus heterogeneity in foetal skeletal muscle
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle is organized into functional domains with attachments at both extremities to tendons via the myotendinous junction (MTJ) and innervation in the middle via the neuromuscular junction (NMJ). papers.abstract: Malignant rhabdoid tumors (MRTs) are lethal, yet genomically simple childhood cancers characterised by universal SWI/SNF dysregulation. Despite this shared molecular framework, the regulatory programs sustaining MRTs and how they wire actionable dependencies, remain poorly defined. We identified recurrent transcriptional metaprograms conserved across patients and molecular subtypes, including a previously undescribed shared core rhabdoid program, as well as a metaprogram characterized by extracellular matrix interactions, and preferentially localized in tumor-stroma intermixed neighborhoods, supporting identification of niche conditioning cues. Mechanistically, we identified regulatory wiring driving these metaprograms, with the core shared rhabdoid programme coordinated by a circuit centred on TCF12, ZNF148 and CHD2. Guided by target nominations from our integrated analyses, we performed a curated drug screen using patient-derived MRT models and validated HGF/MET signaling as a selective vulnerability in extrarenal rhabdoid tumors. Pharmacologic MET inhibition was cytotoxic in sensitive models and induced a complete response in vivo using a clinically approved compound. Importantly, MET expression in primary tumors correlated with response, supporting biomarker-guided patient stratification for immediate clinical translation. Collectively, our findings define the molecular architecture of MRTs, reveal conserved regulatory programs beyond anatomical and molecular subtypes, and highlight a targetable signaling axis with immediate translational potential, establishing a framework for precision therapy in this lethal pediatric malignancy. Drug screening and functional validation identify core regulatory circuit-linked HGF/MET axis dependence in a subset of MRTs. Treatment with a clinically approved MET inhibitor induces striking complete response in vivo in MET-high tumors, supporting MET IHC-guided patient selection and immediate therapeutic translation.

papers.title: Mechanical Distraction Engages a Neuro-Immune Program to Drive Regenerative Soft-Tissue Healing in Ilizarov Bone Transport.
papers.abstract: The Ilizarov bone transport technique reproducibly accelerates soft-tissue healing around the distraction zone through an unexplained mechanism. Local strain was not measured, and direct mechanotransduction at the cellular level remains to be demonstrated. These findings indicate that Ilizarov-type distraction engages a sensory neuro-immune program that orchestrates inflammation resolution and soft-tissue regeneration, providing a mechanistic framework for a long-standing clinical observation.

papers.title: CausalCellInfer: Prioritizing Cell-Type-Specific Disease Associations From Genetically Predicted Transcriptomes in Biobank Cohorts.
papers.abstract: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing(scRNA-seq) with the phenotypic depth of population-scale biobanks is essential for elucidating the cellular basis of complex diseases. CausalCellInfer employs an invariant causal prediction-inspired method(scRNA-seq-based invariant generalized covariance measure, scI-GCM) to select environment-stable marker genes, a parsimonious deep neural network for cell-fraction deconvolution, and regularized matrix completion to reconstruct cell-type-specific (CTS) expression profiles. Inferred CTS differential expression patterns showed significant concordance with independent single-cell studies and were enriched for Open Targets disease genes. papers.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Dentistry: Promise, Pitfalls, and Evidence Gaps.
papers.abstract: GLP-1RAs (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists) have become one of the fastest-growing drug classes worldwide, with prescriptions for obesity treatment increasing by 587% from 2019 to 2024. While their metabolic and cardiovascular benefits are well established, the implications for oral health remain largely unexamined. Preclinical evidence consistently demonstrates anti-inflammatory and osteoprotective effects on periodontal and peri-implant tissues: GLP-1RAs promote osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells, reduce alveolar bone resorption in animal models of periodontitis, and enhance implant osseointegration in diabetic rats. However, these findings are based exclusively on in vitro and animal studies, with only a single retrospective cohort study providing limited clinical data. Conversely, several oral adverse effects have been reported based on pharmacovigilance analyses, including xerostomia, dysgeusia, and anosmia, particularly for semaglutide. Gastrointestinal side effects, particularly nausea (15% to 50%), vomiting (5% to 24%), and gastroesophageal reflux, pose a plausible but unquantified risk for tooth erosion and secondary caries. A bidirectional link between GLP-1 signaling and the oral microbiota, mediated by bacterial dipeptidyl peptidase (DPP)-4-like enzymes that degrade endogenous GLP-1, adds further complexity. Despite this breadth of potential interactions, no prospective study has used any dental outcome as an endpoint in patients receiving GLP-1RAs. This critical appraisal synthesizes the evidence across multiple dental disciplines, grades it in each domain, and identifies the gaps that demand urgent investigation.

papers.title: A nanostructured gradient Ta-O-F barrier-reservoir coating on 316L stainless steel coordinates anti-infective and osteoregenerative responses.
papers.abstract: Early-stage bacterial infection and inadequate osseointegration remain major causes of failure of orthopedic 316L stainless steel (316L SS) implants. Herein, a nanostructured gradient Ta-O-F coating was constructed on 316L SS by stepwise plasma modification: an outer Ta2O5-rich region served as a corrosion-stable barrier, whereas an underlying fluoride-containing region functioned as an ion reservoir, thereby suppressing burst fluoride release and sustaining subsequent exposure. The regulated coating also enhanced endothelial migration and tube formation, while promoting osteoblastic adhesion, proliferation, ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and related gene expression in vitro. These findings establish a barrier-reservoir strategy for coordinating early anti-infective protection with subsequent osteoregenerative responses on metallic implants.

papers.title: Applications and mechanisms of therapeutic ultrasound in skin repair and regeneration.

papers.title: PLA2G2A across tumor compartments and its relevance to drug resistance.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance in cancer is shaped not only by tumor-cell-intrinsic mutations but also by spatially organized microenvironmental states. The pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cancer-associated fibroblast study provides the strongest resistance-proximal immune-functional evidence, whereas mucinous colorectal extracellular vesicles, ovarian ascites, invasive-front fibroblasts, treatment-remodeled stroma and prognostic signatures require more direct therapy-response validation. Gastric and intestinal epithelial data further caution that PLA2G2A may accompany differentiation, invasion restraint, antimicrobial defense or barrier protection. We therefore argue against treating PLA2G2A as a universal oncogenic target. Instead, it should be advanced as a mechanism-matched biomarker or therapeutic hypothesis only when compartment, biochemical-output, functional and perturbational evidence converge.

papers.title: Public omics data reuse in gastric cancer: from discovery abundance to translational evidence.
papers.abstract: Public-omics data are now widely reused in gastric cancer bioinformatics. Resources such as The Cancer Genome Atlas stomach adenocarcinoma cohort (TCGA-STAD), the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), cBioPortal, proteogenomic cohorts, single-cell atlases, and spatial datasets make secondary analysis fast and inexpensive. They are used to study tumor biology, biomarkers, prognosis, therapy-response hypotheses, and tumor-microenvironment states. A major limitation in this literature is not data access. They then produce additional gene lists or risk signatures without a corresponding improvement in independent validation, interpretation, or clinical relevance. The second aim is to use prognostic modeling as a stress test for leakage, overfitting, weak validation, and overinterpreted clinical value. The third aim is to propose GC-PROVE, a five-domain appraisal framework covering problem anchoring, resource provenance, omics workflow transparency, validation hierarchy, and evidence restraint. Public-omics research is most useful when it produces auditable evidence, external validation, biological triangulation, and a clear clinical context.

papers.title: Pericyte-mediated intercellular crosstalk in renal fibrosis: regulatory mechanisms and intervention strategies.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease continues to increase in global prevalence, with renal fibrosis serving as a major pathological driver of end-stage renal disease and imposing a substantial burden on global public health. This process promotes capillary rarefaction and aberrant extracellular matrix deposition, thereby establishing a vicious cycle of "vascular loss-exacerbated hypoxia-progressive fibrosis". Additionally, recent advances in intervention strategies targeting pericyte-mediated crosstalk are critically appraised according to the directness of pericyte targeting and the strength of the supporting evidence, encompassing mesenchymal stem cell therapy, engineered extracellular vesicles, nanomedicine-based drug delivery systems, and natural pharmaceutical therapies. Current evidence remains constrained by the lack of pericyte-specific markers, the reliance on rodent models, and the predominantly preclinical stage of available interventions; nevertheless, a comprehensive understanding of the pericyte-mediated cellular interactome may provide an important theoretical foundation and candidate therapeutic targets for the prevention and treatment of renal fibrosis.

papers.title: ARCADE disentangles cell abundance from continuous transcriptional state in spatial transcriptomics

papers.title: NRF2 in hypertrophic scarring: A stage-dependent redox hub poised between resolution and persistence.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scarring (HTS) is a fibroproliferative outcome of deep dermal injury, reflecting failed scar resolution rather than collagen excess alone. Sustained oxidative and inflammatory signaling is a prominent feature of HTS. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) amplify TGF-β/Smad and NF-κB-linked signaling, reinforce matrix stiffening, and sustain activated fibroblasts within a mechanically loaded niche. However, how NRF2 activity changes across scar maturation-and whether it remains protective, represents a compensatory response, or supports fibroblast persistence-remains unresolved. The KEAP1-NRF2 pathway is a major redox-regulatory node, coordinating antioxidant, detoxification, metabolic, proteostatic, and anti-ferroptotic programs. We propose a testable, stage- and compartment-dependent model rather than a fixed early-to-late switch. Early injury may preferentially engage the redox-sensitive Neh2-KEAP1 arm, whereas growth-factor and mechanical signaling in established scars may increasingly influence NRF2 through the KEAP1-independent Neh6-GSK-3β/β-TrCP arm. Autophagy-linked phospho-p62 (SQSTM1) may provide a separate noncanonical but KEAP1-dependent route to NRF2 stabilization. We synthesize TGF-β/Smad-NOX4 signaling, NF-κB inflammation, p62 feedback, iron-lipid redox and ferroptosis, and mechanoredox coupling-and apply a non-ordinal engagement-to-phenotype (E2P) framework considering disease proximity, NRF2 engagement, causal dependence, scar-relevant phenotype, and replication/methodological quality. Because stage- and cell-resolved nuclear NRF2 data in human HTS are lacking, and disease-proximal evidence for persistence-permissive activity remains limited despite a recent independent gain-/loss-of-function study in human HTS fibroblasts, NRF2 is best viewed as a conditional redox hub rather than a uniformly antifibrotic switch. This framework identifies experiments needed to resolve NRF2 directionality and determine whether stage- and compartment-aware local modulation is therapeutically justified.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics and AI for decoding tumor heterogeneity: implications for target discovery and therapy resistance.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity remains a major bottleneck for effective cancer therapy because many determinants of target expression, biomarker performance, and treatment resistance are spatially organized within the tumor ecosystem. Bulk molecular profiling averages these signals across cell populations, whereas dissociation-based single-cell approaches disrupt the tissue architecture that shapes cell state, signaling, and drug access. Spatial multi-omics addresses these limitations by mapping transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and epigenomic features in situ, while AI enables integration of these modalities with histology, spatial coordinates, and clinical outcomes. Current evidence suggests that graph-based and neighborhood-aware models are most useful for spatial domain detection and niche mapping, whereas multimodal and histology-based models require stronger external validation before clinical deployment. In this review, we examine how spatial multi-omics and AI are redefining tumor heterogeneity as a translational variable in oncology. We focus on target discovery, patient stratification, and resistance biology. We also discuss major barriers to clinical translation, including platform bias, FFPE compatibility, assay cost, molecular coverage, segmentation and registration errors, limited benchmarking, domain shift, and the need for independent multicenter validation.

papers.title: Gestational reorganization of cellular niches and communication revealed by a spatially resolved transcriptional atlas of the macaque maternal-fetal interface
papers.abstract: Reorganization of the cellular composition and cell-signaling networks of the maternal–fetal interface (MFI) occurs across primate gestation. This transition occurs within each trophoblast subtype and is therefore not attributable to their changing abundance. Deconvolution against first trimester and term human references recovered trophoblast identities consistently but assigned maternal and immune identities in a reference-dependent manner, indicating that the gestational stage of a human reference is a determinant of apparent cross-species correspondence. The inferred signaling networks identified here provide a framework for discovering physiological changes across gestation that can be tested in future studies. Overall, this transcriptomic atlas provides a stage-aware resource for translational macaque studies of placental injury, infection, and insufficiency.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omic atlas profiles early organogenesis of a Carnegie stage 12 human embryo.
papers.abstract: Organogenesis marks one of the most dynamic periods of early human embryonic development. papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small plant samples for 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics. Using maize seedling shoot apices as the target, this protocol includes preparation of custom molds for optimal cutting temperature embedding, rapid fresh sample embedding, serial cryosectioning, section-position marking for Visium HD workflows, and morphological quality assessment of replicate tissue slides before transcript capture. The associated data analysis workflow includes Space Ranger processing, Seurat-based normalization and Harmony integration, anatomical domain annotation, pseudobulk and developmental trend analyses, RNA velocity, pseudotime analysis, transcription factor network analysis, single-cell reference mapping, and 3D transcriptome reconstruction. This computational workflow was developed and tested using maize Visium V1 data, but not Visium HD data. This protocol was used to generate serial spatial transcriptomes of maize shoot apices and developing leaf primordia, enabling reconstruction of gene expression transitions from the shoot apical meristem to sequential leaf developmental stages. The approach is also applicable to other small plant tissues, including Arabidopsis first true leaves and Marchantia thalli. Key features • Optimized cryo-embedding and cryosectioning workflow for small plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics. • A streamlined computational workflow for serial-section processing, spatial-domain annotation, 3D reconstruction, and developmental trajectory analysis.

papers.title: Bulk RNA sequencing deconvolution of early-onset pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma identifies cancer-associated fibroblast subsets associated with survival and tumor microenvironment composition.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a lethal cancer characterized by a high abundance of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which influence therapy response, tumor biology and tumor aggressiveness. No associations were observed between mutational signatures and the abundance of CAF and epithelial tumor subtypes. Interestingly, a high abundance of CAFs, and specifically increased iCAF abundance, was associated with improved survival. papers.title: Whole-transcriptome single-cell spatial landscape of instability in human carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: AimsCarotid atherosclerotic plaque instability is a major cause of ischemic stroke. papers.title: The neuro-metabolic-immune axis in breast cancer: emerging mechanisms and subtype-specific therapeutic opportunities.

papers.title: Same organ, divergent immunity: T-cell exhaustion versus stromal exclusion in hepatocellular carcinoma and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

papers.title: Immunomodulation and biofilm disruption of piezoelectric materials in bone infection.
papers.abstract: Bone infection remains a persistent clinical challenge due to biofilm formation, antibiotic resistance, and impaired bone regeneration. papers.title: Encapsulation-integrated microneedle platforms for alopecia treatment: a review of controlled drug delivery, immunomodulation, and hair follicle regeneration.
papers.abstract: Alopecia is a multifactorial disorder characterized by progressive hair loss, follicular dysfunction, and, in some cases, immune-mediated damage, significantly affecting patient quality of life. Although conventional therapies such as topical minoxidil, corticosteroids, and oral immunomodulators remain widely used, their clinical efficacy is often limited by poor skin penetration, short therapeutic duration, systemic adverse effects, and the need for frequent administration. In recent years, microneedle-based platforms have emerged as promising minimally invasive systems capable of enhancing transdermal delivery directly to the follicular microenvironment. This review explores the emerging design space of microneedle platforms integrated with advanced encapsulation strategies for alopecia treatment, with particular emphasis on their roles in immunomodulation and tissue regeneration. By examining the interplay between material composition, carrier architecture, and release behavior, we discuss how these systems improve localized delivery while enabling sustained and controlled therapeutic exposure within the hair follicle niche. Recent advances in nanoparticles, nanoliposomes, porous materials, and microsphere-integrated microneedles, as well as light-guiding systems, have expanded the capabilities of conventional polymeric microneedles beyond passive drug delivery. These platforms enhance drug stability, regulate release kinetics, improve follicular targeting, and actively modulate key biological processes associated with alopecia pathogenesis and regeneration. Reported therapeutic effects include suppression of inflammatory signaling pathways, regulation of immune-cell infiltration, stimulation of angiogenesis, reduction of oxidative stress, activation of follicular stem-cell populations, and promotion of the telogen-to-anagen transition. Collectively, these advances position encapsulation-integrated microneedle systems as a promising class of next-generation therapeutic platforms capable of combining localized delivery with biological microenvironment modulation. papers.title: An Infusible Decellularized Extracellular Matrix Material Binds to Vasculature in Infarcted Myocardium and Induces Pro-Reparative Gene Expression Following Acute Myocardial Infarction Through Inherent Avidity and Bioactive Signaling.

Though mass spectrometry showed similar compositions, biochemical analysis and transmission electron microscopy revealed higher sGAG content within the nanofibrillar high MW, while the globular low MW had more exposed functional groups. These differences translated to a higher binding efficiency of the high MW to ECM proteins and cell surface receptors under flow, while the low MW drove the reduction in vascular permeability. Neither component alone achieved the infarct retention levels of complete iECM, showing that the two components exhibit dependent infarct localization and both are necessary for iECM's overall function. Via single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, both components elicited comparable immunomodulatory and pro‑reparative transcriptional profiles, suggesting that the similarity in composition likely drives the transcriptional response. These findings elucidate the material properties of an intravascularly deliverable ECM biomaterial and how those properties relate to downstream biological behavior, enabling future work investigating nanomaterial mimicry and improvements in material processing and potency.

papers.title: CellChat Hotspot: A Targeted Approach to Cell Cell Communication Analysis With Spatial transcriptomics Validation.
papers.abstract: Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks. This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Applied to stage II colon cancer data, CellChat Hotspot enabled the identification of condition-specific interaction patterns associated with recurrence. Non recurrent patients showed enrichment of immune related processes, whereas recurrent cases were characterized by pathways associated with invasion and metastasis. Notably, a loss of interaction in the HSPG pathway between CALB1+ and stromal cells was observed in recurrent patients, suggesting a potential disruption of cell matrix adhesion mechanisms. To verify the reliability of this finding, we applied the framework to spatial transcriptomics data, which confirmed the presence of the HSPG2 DAG1 interaction in non-recurrent tumors and its near absence in recurrent ones. Overall, this framework provides a biologically guided strategy for studying intercellular communication in complex systems such as the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Postpartum resource scarcity reshapes maternal care, offspring prioritization, and the steroid-sensitive medial preoptic area
papers.abstract: Parental care requires balancing offspring needs with environmental constraints, yet how resource scarcity alters the organization of maternal responses remains poorly understood. Here, we examined maternal behavior, offspring prioritization, and steroid receptor-associated extracellular matrix organization in postpartum rats exposed to limited bedding and nesting (LBN) or control conditions with ample nesting materials. LBN increased pup-directed and reduced self-directed behaviors but also increased behavioral entropy, a measure of behavioral fragmentation, indicating less predictable caregiving sequences. LBN dams preferentially retrieved male pups first, whereas control dams preferentially retrieved females first. LBN also increased the proportion of pup-investigation time directed toward males compared with controls. In offspring on postnatal day 10, corticosterone was elevated in female but not male LBN pups, a pattern that paralleled the maternal male bias. To identify associated neurobiological changes, we assessed steroid receptors and extracellular matrix organization in the medial preoptic area (mPOA), a key region for maternal behavior. LBN increased numbers of estrogen receptor (ER)- and androgen receptor (AR)-immunoreactive cells, reduced perineuronal net (PNN) abundance, and decreased receptor-positive cell enwrapment. Because PNNs constrain structural plasticity, these findings suggest that the postpartum environment alters the organization of steroid receptor-associated extracellular matrix, potentially modulating experience-dependent plasticity in neurosteroid-sensitive circuits. In sum, LBN increases the levels of maternal engagement while reshaping its temporal organization and allocation, accompanied by selective remodeling of steroid-sensitive preoptic architecture. Therefore, maternal adaptation to adversity may be better understood as changes in caregiving allocation strategies rather than a simple gain or loss of maternal care.

papers.title: Ksp37 is a rapidly mobilized NK cell secretory protein that engages FGF2
papers.abstract: A key feature of natural killer (NK) cells is their preloaded arsenal of effector molecules, allowing them to rapidly respond upon activation. In this study, we characterized a previously unexplored secretory protein, termed killer-specific secretory protein of 37 kDa (Ksp37), which is highly abundant in differentiated CD56dim NK cells. Ksp37 is rapidly secreted in a dose-dependent and JAK-1 dependent manner upon low levels of cytokine stimulation, making it a sensitive readout for NK cell activation. Following secretion, intracellular levels were rapidly replenished, preserving responsiveness to subsequent cytokine stimulation. We found that Ksp37 is stored in polarized intracellular compartments distinct from those containing canonical cytotoxic effector molecules, including granzyme B and perforin, which require stronger stimulation for release. Lastly, we identified Ksp37 as a novel binding partner of fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2). This opens new avenues of exploration for the role of NK cells in remodeling their extracellular environment by modulating the FGF2-FGFR1 axis, which plays a key role in tumor growth, angiogenesis and tissue repair.

papers.title: Endogenous expression of mutant RagC in mice results in early-onset dilated cardiomyopathy with features of the Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome
papers.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a severe heart condition often linked to arrhythmias, clots, and heart failure, for which treatments are not yet curative. Recently, de novo mutations in genes encoding components of the Rag GTPase nutrient signaling pathway, particularly in RRAGC, have been found in unrelated patients with a severe, early-onset DCM syndrome called Long-Olsen-Distelmaier. Cancer cell lines, hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and zebrafish have been used to study this Ragopathy, but a mammalian model to investigate this syndrome has not been generated. Here, we show that mice engineered to endogenously express mutations in Serine 74 (orthologous to the Serine 75 mutated in patients), exhibit early-onset features of DCM with decreased heart size, fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction and aortic insufficiency, characteristics reminiscent of the human syndrome. Moreover, Rragc-mutant hearts display decreased left ventricular mass and interventricular septum. Endogenous heterozygous expression of Rragc mutant variants result in a milder, sublethal defective physiological cardiac growth with increased systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Mechanistically, active RagC does not cause abnormal increase in cardiomyocyte size, but leads to suppressed transcriptional activity of Tfeb and alterations in cardiomyocyte metabolism. Transcriptional profiling of neonatal mutant hearts reveals multiple signatures of impaired mitochondrial activity. Ex vivo and in vitro analyses of murine cardiomyocyte mitochondria from Rragc-mutant mice show suppressed mitochondrial respiration, disturbed complex IV multimerization and super-complex organization. These data point to abnormal early postnatal heart metabolism by deregulated nutrient - Rag GTPase signaling with a potential molecular explanation to the early onset of DCM in patients with de novo missense mutations in RRAGC, and suggests the relevance of early metabolic interventions in conditions with altered nutrient signaling

papers.title: DemuxHMM: Large-Scale Single-Cell Embryo Profiling via Recombination Barcoding
papers.abstract: High-resolution developmental time-courses with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) increasingly target trajectory inference and other analyses in the study of development and disease. To address these limitations, we introduce a computational framework for demultiplexing large-scale, individual-resolved datasets. papers.title: Self-organized criticality in a mammalian RNA-interference circuit
papers.abstract: Living systems have been argued to operate near critical points, but their relevance at the cellular level is poorly understood. Critical states allow for a high sensitivity to external inputs and maximal information transfer and display fluctuations at all scales. Critical points are very special, and require the fine tuning of a control parameter, which is hard to reconcile with the robustness of living cells. Self-organized criticality (SOC) proposes that feedback, rather than tuning, brings a system to its critical point. Here we show that RNA interference, in which messenger RNAs compete for shared silencing machinery and so queue for service, together with negative feedback gives rise to SOC in mammalian cells. In a synthetic circuit, a protein repressor whose mRNA competes with the mRNA of a fluorescent reporter that it represses senses the congestion of the queue, closing the feedback loop. Theory and stochastic simulations show that the loop holds the queue near its critical point despite changes in its parameters, and that expression becomes intermittent, with scale-free bursts. Measurements in human cell lines show the predicted power-law distributions of single-cell fluorescence. RNA interference could thus support engineered SOC in animal cells and may also contribute to SOC in natural systems.

papers.title: Genetics and genomics of enteroarthroconidial development in Coccidioides
papers.abstract: Regulated cell death is a cornerstone of plant and animal development. Distant orthologs of some cell death genes are also found in microbes, with roles that remain incompletely understood. The human fungal pathogen Coccidioides causes the disease Valley fever when infectious spores called enteroarthroconidia are inhaled from soil. These spores develop via an unusual checkerboard-style differentiation in which alternating segments of hyphae (cellular filaments) die and disarticulate, releasing mature spores on either side. The molecular mechanisms are unknown. We first adapted single-cell transcriptomics for filamentous fungi, cataloguing expression across the specialized cells of a developing Coccidioides colony. With the resulting profiles, and cell-biological validation via protein tagging, we characterized high expression of the pyroptosis-like cell death pathway in hyphal segments destined to die. Next, we tested the function of pyroptosis-like pathway genes directly by genetic knockout; strains lacking these factors exhibited a phenotype of developmental arrest at a late stage in the colony, preserving hyphal growth but abrogating cell death and spore production. Together, these findings reveal the pyroptosis-like pathway as a requirement for enteroarthroconidial development, and thus infectivity, in Coccidioides. We propose that regulated cell death may prove to mediate events in development in many fungi with multicellular life cycles.

papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies (DEEs) encompass a clinically and molecularly heterogeneous group of mainly genetic disorders. Comprehensive variant analysis included small nucleotide variants (SNVs), indels, SVs, and short tandem repeats. To identify the diagnostic yield of each method, we compared lrGS, srGS and ES re-analysis, and evaluated the additional value of RNA sequencing. Results: We established a diagnosis in 21 of 124 families (16.9%). Fourteen variants were retrospectively detectable in prior ES., Two cases with non-coding variants in SCN1A and RNU2-2 were detectable by both srGS and lrGS. Five SVs also required genome sequencing (5.6% of the total cohort), three of which could be detected, but not confidently resolved by srGS due to breakpoint complexity, repeat-mediated rearrangements, and large copy-neutral events: LrGS enabled accurate characterization of Alu-mediated CDKL5 and STXBP1 deletions and a MEF2C deletion with large inversion. A copy-neutral SCN1A inversion was well characterizable by both srGS and lrGS. One balanced translocation t(X;17) disrupting CDKL5 was resolved by lrGS (srGS unavailable). In addition, ZNF569 and ZNF570 emerged as candidate epilepsy genes from our cohort. Discussion: In ES-negative DEE, the incremental diagnostic yield of genome sequencing was modest, while lrGS provided particular value for the structural resolution of complex rearrangements, especially those involving repetitive sequences. The finding that two-thirds of diagnoses were retrospectively detectable in prior ES highlights the substantial value of systematic reanalysis. Further gains from genome sequencing may increasingly depend on improved interpretation of non-coding variation and integration of long-read-specific information. Our findings indicate that complex SVs represent the class for which lrGS currently yields the most distinctive diagnostic information.

papers.title: Curvature-based schedule ordering is preserved in homogeneous and heterogeneous tumors
papers.abstract: During treatment, dosing protocols with identical total dose may favor one schedule over another depending on how exposure is distributed over time. In homogeneous cell populations, Jensen's inequality has been shown to predict whether continuous or intermittent high-dose followed by low-dose is favored, based on the curvature of the concentration-effect function. Scheduling ordering can be performed based on curvature only: concave functions favor continuous dosing while convex functions favor intermittent dosing schedules with a high time-variance. However, tumors exhibit heterogeneous drug sensitivities, and treatment preferentially eliminates drug-sensitive cells, progressively shifting the surviving population toward greater drug resistance. Whether this treatment-induced selection can reverse curvature-based schedule ordering remains unclear. We develop a mathematical framework in which phenotypes share a common concentration-effect function but differ by fixed, nonnegative sensitivity scales. We prove that the ordering of equal-mean schedules is administrated solely by the scalar cumulative treatment effect, that is, by the curvature of the effect function alone. Consequently, baseline heterogeneity and treatment-induced selection can alter the magnitude of treatment response and the composition of surviving cells, but cannot reverse the ordering of equal-mean schedules predicted by the curvature of the single-cell concentration-effect function. This preservation holds across different temporal dosing profiles and repeated treatment cycles. Our work uncovers a general principle that curvature-based schedule ordering is preserved in heterogeneous tumors despite treatment-induced selection toward resistance.

papers.title: Deciphering the Dynamics of Leukemogenic Transformation from Clonal Hematopoiesis in Congenital Neutropenia
papers.abstract: Inherited neutropenia syndromes, severe congenital neutropenia (CN) and Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS), confer a high cumulative risk of MDS and AML.
