ASXL1 mutations most frequently co-occurred with CSF3R mutations. Co-occurring CSF3R and TP53 mutations were only found in SRP54-CN and CLPB-CN patients. In SDS, TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene, followed by low-prevalence somatic mutations in DNMT3A, IDH1, PTPN11, and RUNX1. In CN-MDS/AML, RUNX1 and SETBP1 mutations emerged shortly before progression to MDS/AML, and membrane-proximal CSF3R mutations only at the leukemic stage. In SDS, biallelic TP53-mutant clones expanded prior to transformation, and a variant allele frequency (VAF) of dominant TP53 clone above 0.074 discriminated between patients who progressed and those who did not. Peripheral blood reflected bone marrow genotype for most key drivers. Leukemic transformation in inherited neutropenia is therefore not stochastic, but rather follows a defined mutational sequence, initiated in childhood.

papers.title: Single-nucleus analysis reveals renal STAT1/CEBPB signaling as a modifiable relay of proinflammatory FGF23 effects in diabetic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Background Circulating fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises dramatically in chronic kidney disease, particularly in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). papers.title: Cxcr2 is required for ductal outgrowth and shapes the stromal microenvironment in postnatal mammary gland development
papers.abstract: Mammary gland development requires coordinated signaling between epithelial and stromal compartments. papers.title: scDeepSim: Deep Generative Simulation for Controlled Benchmarking of Single-Cell Methods
papers.abstract: Benchmarking single-cell computational methods requires both realistic data and reliable ground truth. However, annotating real datasets is costly and, even when available, may not fully represent the diverse settings where methods are used. Simulators address this gap by generating synthetic data that has fully specified ground truth and whose structure can be tailored to challenge competing methods. Existing single-cell simulators can broadly be divided into statistical and deep generative classes. Statistical simulators offer interpretable parameters for controlling simulated data, but their modeling assumptions may not accurately represent real data. Deep generative models can learn complex expression patterns, but it remains unclear how to transparently control individual biological or technical factors without introducing unintended effects. We introduce scDeepSim, a simulator that combines a structured variational autoencoder with latent diffusion to generate synthetic single-cell expression profiles. It allows users to intervene on selected biological or technical factors at user-specified strengths, producing realistic datasets with benchmark ground truth. We demonstrate this capability by benchmarking batch correction and trajectory inference methods, showing how batch-effect strength affects batch mixing and cell-type preservation, and how trajectory geometry and noise affect pseudotime recovery. scDeepSim therefore enables researchers to vary selected biological and technical factors in realistic simulated data and assess how these changes affect the performance of single-cell analysis methods, helping understand when such methods may be appropriately applied. Code for the scDeepSim simulator and experiments is available at https://github.com/LangtianM/scDeepSim.

papers.title: Where the magnet sits sets the sign of the scaling law: membrane-anchored versus intracellular magnetic actuation of cells
papers.abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles apply mechanical force to cells in two incompatible geometries: anchored to the plasma membrane, where a rotating field twists a surface-bound cap, and internalized into lysosomes, where an assembled rod stirs the organelle lumen. Treated analytically at matched single-cell magnetic moment, the step-out frequency of an intracellular rod falls with assembly size while that of a membrane cap rises linearly; the scaling exponents have opposite sign and the curves cross at 184 particles and 4.04 Hz, inside the window in which published experiments operate. The model reproduces four published measurements with no fitted parameters. One disagrees: our intralysosomal wall shear stress is 33 to 81 times below the published value while reproducing every structural feature of it. The model yields two zero-predictions that one experiment would falsify.

papers.title: A protocol for cortical and deep-brain calcium imaging in freely moving mice with the Mini2P system.
papers.abstract: Two-photon calcium imaging has transformed our understanding of neuronal circuit function, yet conventional approaches require head fixation, limiting the study of neural activity during natural behavior. Designed for adaptation across brain regions and behavioral paradigms, the protocol provides practical guidance for identifying technical challenges and verifying successful implementation. By establishing clear decision points, validation criteria, and troubleshooting strategies at each stage, this workflow aims to improve reproducibility and facilitate the adoption of the Mini2P for investigating neuronal circuit dynamics during freely moving behavior.

papers.title: Scientific Figure Library connects visual examples with reusable plotting code

papers.title: The Reasoning Paradox in Scientific Sandboxes: Why Extended Reasoning Fails in Autonomous Bioinformatics and How to Fix It.
papers.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) trained with extended reasoning, such as DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI o1, have established state-of-the-art benchmarks in formal logic, competitive programming, and mathematics. papers.title: MorphoANOVA: Dissecting Histology-Gene Expression Relationships in Spatial Transcriptomics

papers.title: Simple models outperform single-cell foundation models on downstream benchmarks
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data exhibit strong and reproducible statistical structure. This has motivated the development of large-scale foundation models, such as TranscriptFormer, that use transformer-based architectures to learn a generative model for gene expression by embedding genes into a latent vector space. These embeddings have been used to obtain state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on downstream tasks such as cell-type classification, disease-state prediction, and cross-species learning. Here, we ask whether similar performance can be achieved without utilizing computationally intensive deep learning-based representations. Using simple, interpretable pipelines that rely on careful normalization and linear methods, we obtain SOTA or near SOTA performance across multiple benchmarks commonly used to evaluate single-cell foundation models, including outperforming foundation models on out-of-distribution tasks involving novel cell types and organisms absent from the training data. Our findings highlight the need for rigorous benchmarking and suggest that the biology of cell identity can be captured by simple linear representations of single cell gene expression data.

papers.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response

papers.title: KLONE: An Imbalance-Robust k-NN Ensemble for Cross-Modal Single-Cell Clone Assignment

KLONE is the most accurate method and recalls minority clones at 100\%. papers.title: Development of a Thyroid Cancer to Lung Metastasis-on-a-Chip Model
papers.abstract: Background: Study of the metastatic cascade in differentiated non-medullary thyroid cancer (NMTC) is hampered by the relative lack of preclinical models that metastasize from primary tumors to other organs. We previously identified regulator of calcineurin 1 isoform 4 (RCAN1.4) as a suppressor of NMTC cell growth, invasion, and metastasis using in vitro systems and tail vein injections in immunocompromised mice. We then reported a microfluidic device mimicking the mouse tail vein injection where cancer cells were allowed to flow directly to lung organoid constructs. We now report the development of a full primary tumor to lung metastasis-on-a-chip (MOC) model for TC. Methods: Resin molds for primary and secondary sites connected by a channel were 3D printed and filled with polydimethylsiloxane to create a molded silicone elastomer. The primary site was seeded with an organoid composed of a hyaluronic acid and collagen-based hydrogel into which FTC236 and HTh74 NMTC cells with and without knockdown of RCAN1.4 were engrafted. The secondary site consisted of a hydrogel organoid into which bronchial epithelial cells and lung fibroblasts were seeded. Culture media was circulated and movement of NMTC cells to the secondary site was assessed. Results: Both cell lines that expressed RCAN 1.4 metastasized to the secondary lung site. RCAN1.4-reduced FTC236 cells had increased metastatic behavior vs controls while HTh74 was less affected by RCAN1.4 loss, similar to prior studies. To determine if the MOC could be used for incorporation of immune components and therapeutic modeling, NK-92 cells were added and were shown to be reduce metastases for both cell lines in the presence or absence of RCAN1.4. Analysis of MOC circulating fluid revealed elevated levels of granzyme B, consistent with NK-92 cell activation. Cytokine profiling identified elevated probable NMTC and NK-92-derived factors. Conclusions: These results indicate that NMTC metastatic behavior can be modeled using a novel MOC system for mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies.

papers.title: Deep CyTOF immune profiles of ex vivo granulomatous responses to Mycobacterium tuberculosis differ with European and African geographical origin
papers.abstract: Genetic and environmental factors influence human immunity and modulate responses to infection. Accounting for immune heterogeneity across human populations is critical to the design of novel vaccines and host-directed interventions that would optimally benefit populations experiencing the highest disease burden. Tuberculosis (TB) burden is unevenly distributed across geographical regions and our understanding of the differential immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) across human populations remains limited. Here, we sought to evaluate the impact of geographical origin on ex vivo granulomatous responses to Mtbinfection. We found that peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy African donors exhibited greater control of Mtbgrowth ex vivo than those isolated from European individuals. High-dimensional single-cell profiling of the granulomatous responses by cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) revealed divergent profiles based on the specimens' geographical origin. Monocytes from European donors displayed a pro-inflammatory phenotype - correlating with Mtbgrowth -, whereas PBMCs of African individuals were enriched in activated, cytotoxic T cells - correlating with Mtbcontrol. Reduced inflammatory response in African monocytes following various microbial stimulations was confirmed. Taken together, our comprehensive immune profiling indicates that environmental and genetic factors shape a cytotoxic-regulatory response that promotes bacterial control. Against the current "one-treatment-fits-all" approach, our findings support the use of specimens from intervention-relevant settings to inform the targeted design of TB vaccines and host-directed interventions.

papers.title: Identification and localization of bone marrow ILC2s using Id2/Cxcr6 dual-reporter mice
papers.abstract: Type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) are present in the bone marrow, where their identification and spatial localization remain challenging because of their low abundance and the expression of shared markers by other lymphoid populations. Here, we evaluated the use of Id2YFP/+ Cxcr6GFP/+ dual-reporter mice to identify and visualize bone marrow ILC2s. Using spectral flow cytometry, we showed that both ST2- and ST2 ILC2s expressed high levels of ID2, whereas CXCR6 expression differed between these subsets. However, the ID2 expressing compartments also contained NK cells, NKT cells, conventional T cells and ILC progenitors. Surface marker profiling identified CD25 and ICOS as useful markers for enriching ILC2 populations, with ST2 enabling the segregation of the ST2- and ST2 subsets. Single-cell RNA sequencing further characterized the diversity of Id2 and Cxcr6 expressing lymphoid populations and supported the use of CD5 and NKp46 as exclusion markers. Combining these markers with the dual-reporter system, confocal microscopy revealed YFPGFPCD5-NKp46- cells compatible with an ILC2 phenotype, distributed throughout the bone marrow as isolated cells or within multicellular clusters. Complementary flow cytometric analyses demonstrated that ILC2s accounted for more than 90% of a phenotypically related reporter-positive population after exclusion of major T and NK cell populations, providing additional support for the identification of the cells visualized in situ as putative ILC2s. Together, these findings establish a strategy combining dual-reporter mice, flow cytometry, transcriptomic profiling and confocal imaging to investigate the localization and spatial organization of putative bone marrow ILC2s.

papers.title: IL13 critically contributes to the antitumor activity of polyfunctional CD4+ T cells driven by constitutively active Stat5
papers.abstract: The presence of polyfunctional T cells capable of concurrently producing multiple cytokines correlates with favorable clinical outcomes in patients with cancer. We previously reported that overexpression of constitutively active Stat5a (CASTAT5) confers polyfunctionality on tumor-specific CD4 T cells, enabling durable antitumor immunity following adoptive cell therapy. However, the mechanisms underlying the enhanced antitumor effects of CASTAT5-modified T cells remain unclear. Here, we identify interleukin-13 (IL13) as a critical effector cytokine contributing to the multifaceted antitumor activity of CASTAT5-conditioned polyfunctional CD4 T cells (C5-CD4). C5-CD4 T cells exhibit a prominent T helper 2 (Th2) cytokine profile, accompanied by extensive epigenomic remodeling at the Th2 cytokine loci, as revealed by Hi-C and histone-modification CUT&Tag assays. Neutralization of IL13 diminished the antitumor efficacy of C5-CD4 T cells. Furthermore, targeted Il13 disruption substantially impaired tumor control and was associated with reduced donor T cell expansion and persistence, diminished systemic cytokine and chemokine responses, and attenuated activation of endogenous tumor-reactive CD8 T cells. Nonetheless, IL13 overexpression alone in donor CD4 T cells failed to fully recapitulate the therapeutic activity of C5-CD4 T cells, indicating that IL13 is a critical contributor but is insufficient to account for the full antitumor activity conferred by CASTAT5. Single-cell RNA sequencing associated donor-derived IL13 with increased representation of tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells and IL13-signaling in monocytes and macrophages exhibiting tissue-repair-associated transcriptional programs. Moreover, Il13 disruption diminished the therapeutic efficacy of CASTAT5-expressing CD19-targeted CAR-T cells in a mouse B-cell lymphoma model. Reanalysis of a human CD19CAR-T infusion-product dataset further revealed an association between IL13 expression and type 2 cytokine signatures linked to prolonged clinical response, suggesting a potential contribution of IL13 to the efficacy of human CD19CAR-T therapy. Together, these findings uncover an unexpected antitumor role for IL13 and establish it as a critical node linking polyfunctional donor T cells with endogenous immune cells to promote sustained tumor immunity.

papers.title: ProClust provides reliable statistical significance of clusters for single-cell transcriptomic data
papers.abstract: Clustering of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is widely used to identify cell populations. However, overclustering can partition a single cell population into multiple clusters, potentially leading to spurious identification of cell subpopulations. Assessing the statistical significance of clusters is therefore needed to support their biological interpretation. We propose ProClust, a statistical test for clustering significance in scRNA-seq data. ProClust defines a single cluster as a log-concave distribution and adopts a projection-based approach to quantify clustering uncertainty through p-values. These projections can also provide interpretable visual evidence for individual clusterings. ProClust merges clusters when there is insufficient evidence to reject the single-cluster null hypothesis, refining an initial overclustering without prespecifying the final number of clusters. Across parametric and PBMC-based semi-synthetic simulations, ProClust avoided false subdivisions under single-population null settings while consistently recovering the underlying population structure across different numbers of true populations. In real scRNA-seq datasets from the Human Lung Cell Atlas, Tabula Muris, and Hydra, ProClust produced clustering solutions that showed overall agreement with reference annotations while retaining supported substructure and merging groups with insufficient evidence for separation. Together, these results demonstrate that ProClust provides a statistically principled and interpretable framework for refining an initial overclustering and distinguishing supported cellular heterogeneity. The ProClust R package is available at https://github.com/Anonym027/ProClust.

papers.title: Spatial proteomics on repurposed sequencers reveals early astrocytic remodeling in an ALS mouse model
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics can reveal how disease reshapes cells and their local environments, but extending these measurements across replicated tissue cohorts requires validated antibodies, consistent sample processing and integrated analysis. These requirements are particularly pressing in studies of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), where pathology evolves unevenly across spinal-cord regions and disease stages. Here, we established an end-to-end spatial proteomics workflow linking a validated 28-antibody panel to automated fluorescence decoding and imaging on repurposed high-throughput sequencers, followed by multicycle image processing, cellular profiling and probabilistic spatial-neighborhood analysis. We applied it to 70 lumbar spinal-cord sections from nine SOD1-G93A and nine wild-type mice at presymptomatic, disease-onset and symptomatic stages. Spatial neighborhood analysis revealed that the environments surrounding motor neurons were already remodeled at disease onset. GFAP-high neighborhoods expanded in the ventral gray matter, with 43% of motor neurons embedded in these environments in SOD1-G93A mice, compared with 15% in wild-type mice. This early expansion preceded the later decline of non-reactive gray matter and detectable motor-neuron loss. The regional organization of the protein-defined changes shared features with neuronal and astrocytic patterns mapped by spatial transcriptomics in mouse and human ALS. This work enables spatial proteomics across replicated tissue cohorts and identifies localized remodeling of the environments around surviving motor neurons as an early feature of disease in the SOD1-G93A model.

papers.title: Dual CD40/CD28 co-stimulation reprograms the solid-tumor microenvironment to unleash CAR-T and endogenous anti-tumor immunity
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has shown limited efficacy against solid tumors, owing to poor T-cell persistence, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and cancer immune evasion. Here we describe LACO-Stim (lymphocytes-APC co-stimulator), a chimeric co-stimulatory molecule composed of an agonistic anti-CD40 single-chain variable fragment (scFv) and the CD28 intracellular signaling domain, such that a single molecule activates CD40-expressing antigen-presenting cells while delivering CD28 co-stimulation to the T cell that bears it. Co-expressed with a 4-1BB-based CAR (LACO-CAR-T), it enhanced anti-tumor activity in vitro and achieved durable, complete in most mice, tumor regression rather than transient control in xenograft and immunocompetent models. In immunocompetent hosts, LACO-CAR-T activated dendritic cells, reprogrammed tumor macrophages toward M1-like, antigen-presenting states, and induced epitope spreading with endogenous CD8 T-cell responses against tumor neoantigens. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA-velocity analysis revealed coordinated immune remodeling: T cells shifted toward a more stem-like, less terminally exhausted state, regulatory T cells declined in frequency and suppressive function, and myeloid cells acquired antigen-presentation programs while excessive inflammatory and suppressive signaling was restrained. LACO-Stim further synergized with anti-PD-1 blockade to control tumor growth. LACO-Stim thus enables CAR-T cells to coordinate intrinsic T-cell reinforcement with extrinsic immune reprogramming, converting an immunosuppressive TME into a de-inflamed (reduced inflammatory signaling), de-suppressed rather than merely armed niche that supports endogenous anti-tumor immunity.

papers.title: Functional Conservation Amid Extreme Divergence in Freshwater SAR11 Hypervariable Region 2
papers.abstract: The Ca. Pelagibacterales order (SAR11) is a ubiquitous bacterioplankton in aquatic ecosystems. The genomes of SAR11 bacteria contain hypervariable region 2 (HVR2), the largest HVR with extreme diversity. Previous studies collectively indicated the enrichment of cell-surface modification genes on HVR2, which have been hypothesized to facilitate phage evasion. However, characterisation of HVR2 has primarily targeted marine clades and been limited for freshwater SAR11 (aka. Fontibacterium). Here, we employed single-cell genomics and recovered 176 Fontibacterium HVR2 sequences from Lake Biwa (Japan) and Lake Zurich (Switzerland), across multiple sampling years for Lake Biwa. Comparative sequence analyses revealed that freshwater HVR2 showed high intra-population diversity and appears to evolve independently of the rest of the genome, mirroring patterns observed in marine counterparts. Nevertheless, highly conserved HVR2 sequence pairs were observed for distinct Fontibacterium species from the two intercontinental habitats, suggesting horizontal transfers of HVR2 with conserved functional configurations across divergent lineages and large spatial scales. Further comparison with 145 marine HVR2 sequences revealed HVR2 sequences displaying synteny between Fontibacterium and marine SAR11, and 209 gene families conserved across habitats, including three near-universally conserved families. All examined freshwater HVR2s contained initiator methionine tRNA genes concentrated near the boundaries of the 5S region, suggesting a tDNA-anchored integration mechanism. These results suggest the functional equivalence of HVR2 across marine and freshwater SAR11 clades, and the existence of a shared pool of HVR2 sequences that evolve reticulately through mutual genetic exchange, independent of the vertical inheritance of the rest of the genome.

papers.title: Epigenetic Mechanisms Inhibit Smad7 and Contribute to Fibrosis in Crohn's Disease
papers.abstract: Background & Aims: TGF-beta1 is a central regulator of profibrotic gene expression, extracellular matrix deposition, and the development of intestinal fibrosis in patients with fibrostenotic Crohns disease (CD). Unlike the increased expression of Smad7 in mucosal and lamina propria monocytes, where it impairs Treg function, mesenchymal cells from patients with fibrostenotic CD do not exhibit elevated Smad7 expression and instead display sustained TGF-beta1 signaling. We therefore sought to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the unexpected silencing of Smad7 in fibrostenotic CD. Methods: Subepithelial myofibroblasts (SEMFs) and muscularis smooth muscle cells were isolated from paired normal and affected ileal tissues obtained from the same patients with each Montreal phenotype of CD, as well as from non-CD controls. Gene expression, RNA-binding affinity, transcriptional activity, promoter methylation, protein levels, and the mechanisms that regulate Smad7 expression were evaluated in ex vivo tissues and primary cultured cells. MicroRNA-21 (miR-21) localization was assessed by RNAscope. miR-21-mediated suppression of Smad7 was investigated using antagomiR-21. Smad7 silencing through promoter hypermethylation was confirmed using 5-Azacytidine treatment and DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1) knockdown. Smad7 lysine acetylation and Smurf1/2-mediated ubiquitination were examined using selective inhibitors and proximity ligation assays. Results: In SEMFs from patients with fibrostenotic CD, aberrant silencing of Smad7 resulted from DNMT1-dependent promoter hypermethylation and pSmad3-driven, miR-21-mediated degradation of Smad7 mRNA. In addition, Smurf1/2 promoted ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of acetylated Smad7 protein. Inhibition of miR-21 with antagomiR-21 restored Smad7 expression and reduced TGF-beta 1-dependent profibrotic gene expression. Likewise, demethylation with 5-Azacytidine or knockdown of DNMT1 induced Smad7 promoter hypomethylation and restored Smad7 expression. Furthermore, modulation of the balance between p300 acetyltransferase and histone deacetylase 1 (HDAC1) stabilized Smad7 protein by protecting it from degradation. Conclusions: A distinctive pattern of epigenetic silencing and post-translational regulation of Smad7 was identified in patients with fibrostenotic CD. These mechanisms collectively promote unrestrained TGF-beta1 signaling by suppressing Smad7 expression and stability in SEMFs, thereby contributing to the development of intestinal fibrosis.

papers.title: Donor-associated variation outweighs PMOS status in patient-derived iPSC transcriptomes: a genotyped, BMI-adjusted study of 14 lines
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from patients have been little used to model polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS, formerly polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS), and differences between unrelated donors can masquerade as disease effects. Earlier comparisons of three or four donors per group reported hundreds to thousands of differentially expressed genes. We asked whether a disease signature is detectable in a larger, genotyped panel, balanced for BMI category and BMI-adjusted, of full-phenotype patients. Methods: We studied 14 clonal, transgene-free iPSC lines reprogrammed by CRISPR activation from endometrial stromal fibroblasts of seven women with PMOS meeting all three Rotterdam criteria, and seven controls frequency-matched for BMI category (30 kg/m2). Bulk RNA-seq (16,489 expressed genes) was related to diagnosis, hormones, metabolic traits, age, and X-inactive specific transcript (XIST) status using gene-wise models, exact enumeration of all 3,432 group splits, and permutation-calibrated gene-set tests. Donors were genotyped within a cohort of 140 women and scored with an imputation-based genome-wide PMOS polygenic risk score (PRS). PMOS risk-locus genes were examined against a 202-line iPSC proteome. Results: PMOS donors had higher anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), testosterone, and free androgen index than controls. No gene was differentially expressed between PMOS and control lines (false discovery rate < 0.1), and the number of nominally associated genes was no greater than for random 7-versus-7 splits of the lines (p = 0.75). This was unchanged with an alternative read quantification and with count-based models. With seven donors per group, the design could detect 1.8-fold differences per gene, compared with roughly 3- to 6-fold for the three- or four-donor designs used previously. Neither diagnosis nor any hormonal or metabolic trait explained more expression variance than chance, and neither PMOS GWAS-locus genes nor Hallmark pathways were enriched. Two control lines showed near-complete loss of XIST, potentially indicative of X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) erosion, and a third was borderline. Endocrine PMOS-locus genes (e.g., FSHR, AMH) were not expressed, whereas DNA-repair and growth genes were. Across 129 genotyped women, the PRS was higher in PMOS (odds ratio 1.81 per SD; AUC 0.65), but PMOS and control iPSC donors overlapped fully in polygenic risk. Conclusions: In this panel of 14 undifferentiated iPSC lines from women with the full PMOS phenotype, no robust PMOS-associated transcriptomic differences were detected. Expression variation was dominated by line-to-line differences, consistent with donor background as their main source, although with one clone per donor a contribution of clonal variation cannot be excluded. Reduced XIST expression in some control lines is potentially indicative of, but does not establish, X-chromosome inactivation erosion. Disease-associated differences in differentiated, hormone-responsive cells cannot be excluded, and differences reported in smaller panels may partly reflect inter-donor variability. Future studies should use adequately sized panels, control for XIST erosion, select donors by polygenic risk, and examine hormone-responsive derivatives. Keywords: polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome; polycystic ovary syndrome; induced pluripotent stem cells; transcriptome; polygenic risk; XIST erosion; disease modelling; experimental design

papers.title: Comparative larval single-cell transcriptomics provides insights into the evolutionary origins of sensory-neural programmes in Porifera and Cnidaria
papers.abstract: Understanding how specialised cell types emerged and diversified is fundamental to reconstructing animal evolution. The origins of neural and sensory-secretory cell types are particularly intriguing, and early diverging non-neuronal metazoans, such as sponges, provide critical insights into pre-neural molecular toolkits. Free-swimming larval stages of sponges and cnidarians provide an unique context for investigating these questions, as these larvae rely on specialised sensory and signalling systems to detect environmental cues and coordinate behaviour during dispersal and settlement. Here, we integrated larval single-cell transcriptomic datasets from the demosponge Amphimedon queenslandica and four cnidarian species (Nematostella vectensis, Astroides calycularis, Pocillopora acuta and Clytia hemisphaerica). Cross-species mapping using Self-Assembling Manifold mapping (SAMap) recovered broad conservation of major cell-type identities among cnidarians, including neural, secretory, cnidocyte, epithelial, gastrodermal and apical populations. Extending these comparisons to A. queenslandica displayed transcriptional similarities between several sponge larval cell populations and cnidarian neural, sensory and progenitor-associated cell types. Within-species analyses showed that these cell populations remained transcriptionally integrated within the broader epithelial and sensory cell type of the sponge larva. Neural-associated gene modules, including conserved families associated with photoreception, neural fate specification and postsynaptic scaffolding, were distributed across distinct epithelial and sensory-like sponge larval cell populations rather than being restricted to a single proto-neural cell type. Our findings suggest that molecular components subsequently incorporated into neural systems were already deployed across diverse cell types in a common ancestor of sponges & cnidarians. Our work supports an evolutionary scenario in which extant neural and sensory-secretory cell types arose through the diversification and reorganisation of molecular programmes distributed across multiple ancestral sensory-secretory cell types.

papers.title: Getting a head start: Craniofacial heterochrony in marsupials involves dynamic changes to cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying neural crest migration
papers.abstract: The neural crest is a vertebrate innovation central to craniofacial development and evolution. While the gene regulatory networks guiding neural crest development are well characterized, the mechanisms generating species-specific craniofacial diversity remain poorly understood. Marsupials provide a unique model for studying neural crest plasticity, having evolved accelerated patterns of craniofacial development. This adaptation arises because marsupials are born altricial after a short gestation yet require well-developed mouthparts to attach to a teat and continue development in the pouch. However, how marsupials achieve this heterochronic shift in neural crest development is largely unknown. Here we investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying their distinct heterochrony across three marsupial species, with mouse and chicken as comparators. We reveal that marsupials produce dense pre-migratory aggregates of neural crest cells at the borders of a still-flat, pre-neurulation embryo, which emigrate as cohesive, E-cadherin-positive, vimentin-negative epithelial-like sheets, potentially facilitating rapid establishment of the facial prominences. Re-analysis of published marsupial single-cell data further suggests that the mesenchymal transcriptional programme is deployed after delamination and migration. These cellular behaviours have not been described in other amniotes, instead resembling patterns in anamniotes which similarly exhibit accelerated craniofacial development to support early feeding. Marsupials thus appear to have evolved a similar mechanism of neural crest migration to facilitate their developmental heterochrony. These findings suggest that vertebrate neural crest migration may be shaped by life history as well as phylogeny, providing new perspectives on neural crest plasticity and the developmental mechanisms driving craniofacial diversity.

papers.title: A Multidimensional Arithmetical Ontology for High-Parameter Cytometry: Gaussian Primes and Cryptographic Hashing for Cell Population Standardization
papers.abstract: Background. The rapid expansion of high-dimensional single-cell technologies has outpaced the development of standardized metadata infrastructure. Current text-based ontology for cell populations and gating strategies lacks computational rigor, hindering process automation and cross-study reproducibility. Our previous frameworks, the Prime Population System (PPS) and the Unique Gating Identifier (UGI), proposed arithmetical solutions but were limited by biological fragility (no inherent link between a protein and its structural isoforms) and by computational bottlenecks caused by exponential integer growth. Objective. To develop a scalable, multidimensional arithmetical ontology that unambiguously identifies cell populations and hierarchical gating strategies. Methods. We transition the marker dictionary from the one-dimensional real axis (R) to the complex plane of Gaussian integers (a+bi). The reviewed human proteome of the UniProt Knowledgebase is paired with Gaussian primes satisfying a > b > 0. Each protein receives a contiguous reserved block of 64 primes: slot 0 addresses the protein with isoform unresolved, and slot k addresses UniProt isoform k, the slot index being read directly off the accession. Carbohydrate epitopes, which have no UniProt entry, are paired through the CD nomenclature instead: in a CD region beyond the 80,000 blocks reserved for the proteome, each CD number receives a block of 1,024 primes, with the slot read off the suffix of the designation. A bipartite encoding represents positive (a+bi) and negative (b+ai) expression states through Conjugate Pair Symmetry. To avoid the integer explosion of Godel exponentiation, hierarchical gating sequences are held as vectorized arrays of complex numbers and compressed by SHA-256 deterministic hashing. Results. Pairing against the human proteome assigns 53,296 identifiers, 20,431 protein-level and 32,865 isoform-level. Every isoform description resolves under a single rule, including the 329 descriptions whose accession prefix differs from the entry that cites them. The 19 carbohydrate designations of the CD list, CD57 among them, receive identifiers in the CD region. Localized vectorization with SHA-256 hashing yields immutable 64-character hexadecimal fingerprints for entire gating strategies, resolving the integer explosion problem. Conclusion. By combining Gaussian primes with hashing, Gaussian Prime Cytometry provides a scalable, computationally lightweight and biologically accurate identifier system. The system eliminates nomenclature ambiguity and facilitates machine learning applications and centralized global cytometry databases.

papers.title: Uncovering cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial omics
papers.abstract: Individual cells simultaneously encode multiple biological signals in their gene expression profiles, including spatial position, circadian phase, and disease state. These signals can be entangled in complex ways, including circadian patterns that vary along disease progression and cell cycle dynamics that shift along developmental trajectories. While methods to disentangle such signals have been recently developed, characterizing the interaction itself between multicellular signals along with its effects on tissue function, localizing cellular subpopulations which exhibit signal interactions, and identifying potential candidate genes which drive such interactions, all remain major challenges. We present CRISP which characterizes signal interactions in single-cell gene expression data based on the correspondence between the multiple, probabilistic signal-specific projections of the data. Across simulations with tunable couplings and four single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, CRISP recovers diverse biological signal interactions and localizes them to informative cellular subpopulations and groups of associated genes; CRISP distinguishes healthy from fibrotic liver samples and localizes the loss of zonation-position coupling to individual fibrotic hepatocytes, resolves the asymmetric coupling of TGF-{beta} response, EMT, and cell-cycle phase to specific cell subpopulations, and flags transcriptionally delayed hepatocytes in Plasmodium liver infection. Beyond quantifying and localizing signal interactions, CRISP can refine existing labels, uncover continuous cellular transitions and reveal condition-associated genes.

papers.title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network (GRN) inference. To identify where they add value, we benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), CellOracle, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and task-matched simple baselines on the same data, from K562 Perturb-seq screens and primary cells to healthy-donor and isogenic leukodystrophy brain organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and lung cancer biopsies. FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline. Zero-shot in silico perturbations captured the direction of real responses in K562, with up to 75% of perturbations shifted in the expected direction (scFoundation, p < 1e-8), and Geneformer V2 networks recovered patient-level tumour differential expression better than co-expression (fold enrichment 2.9 versus 2.0). Within a species, FM embeddings annotated cells as accurately as principal components. In organoids, predicted knockout effects were largely explained by where the target is expressed, and an expression-matched control test isolated the gene-specific part, 12 to 35% of the effects. Isogenic Canavan and Krabbe organoids and 4H patient organoids, with one library per line and time point, did not yet separate methods from differences between clones and donors, which defines the replication needed for future validation. Fine-tuning changed classification accuracy but not knockout rankings. We release the benchmark, baselines, pipeline checks and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package, so that new models can be evaluated on the tasks where FMs already help.

papers.title: Wealth inequalities in timely postnatal care in Malawi: how much do antenatal care and place of delivery explain?
papers.abstract: Background Postnatal care (PNC) is important for maternal and newborn health, but socioeconomic inequalities may limit timely access. In Malawi, evidence on PNC timing and the pathways linking household wealth to PNC is limited. We examined socioeconomic inequalities in timely PNC and whether antenatal care (ANC) and delivery-facility type accounted for part of the wealth gradient. Methodology We analysed 4,726 women with a live birth in the previous 24 months from the 2024 Malawi Demographic and Health Survey. PNC was timely when the first check occurred within two days of birth, delayed when it occurred later, and absent when no qualifying check was reported. Survey-weighted multinomial logistic regression examined associations between household wealth and PNC timing, with sequential adjustment for maternal education, ANC and place of delivery. The slope index of inequality (SII) and relative index of inequality (RII) summarised inequality. Pathway analyses examined ANC and delivery-facility type as mediators. Results Overall, 66.6% of women received timely PNC, 5.1% delayed PNC and 28.3% no PNC. Unadjusted, women in the richer and richest wealth quintiles had lower relative risk ratios (RRR) of no PNC than women in the poorest quintile (RRR 0.56 and 0.57, respectively). After full adjustment, the richer group remained less likely to have no PNC (RRR 0.67, 95% CI 0.50-0.89). Wealth inequality persisted (SII -8.4 percentage points, 95% CI -14.8 to -2.0; RII 0.74, 95% CI 0.59-0.93). Among all births, 26.6% of the wealth association with no PNC was accounted for by ANC and place of delivery, primarily home delivery. Conclusion Timely PNC remains unequally distributed by household wealth in Malawi. The findings suggest that reducing missed PNC opportunities requires attention to socioeconomic barriers and continuity from pregnancy through delivery and the postnatal period.

papers.title: Engineered microvessel networks -- Longitudinal transcriptomic profiling validates chip-grown tissues as a robust model for studying vasculature
papers.abstract: Vascularised Organ-on-Chip (OoC) models are promising New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), but their translation requires validation for defined Contexts of Use (CoU). Here, we combine microfluidic microvessel networks (MVNs) with longitudinal bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to determine how cell provenance influences engineered vascular phenotype. papers.title: Inference of cell division parameters in bacteria under transient growth conditions
papers.abstract: Most quantitative models of bacterial cell division assume steady-state growth, yet natural environments are highly dynamic. Here, we infer division control parameters of E. coli from single-cell size trajectories under nonsteady growth. We describe growth as a continuous process interrupted by stochastic divisions, whose propensity depends on cell size and on the size added since birth. Combining an estimation of time-dependent single-cell growth rates with a maximum-likelihood estimator that we previously validated on synthetic data, we obtain time-resolved estimates of the mean added size at division, its noise, and a strategy parameter that measures how added size depends on birth size. This parameter vanishes for the adder, in which cells add, on average, a fixed size regardless of their size at birth, and is negative for sizer-adder control, in which larger-born cells add less size. We apply this approach to published single-cell data covering steady exponential growth, gradual nutrient depletion, and exit from starvation. We implement a time-resolved model selection based on the Akaike information criterion, concluding that the adder is sufficient during steady growth, whereas size dynamics during entry into and exit from stationary phase are better explained by transient deviations toward sizer-adder control. The framework provides a general method to quantify time-resolved changes in the scale, stochasticity, and strategy of division in nonsteady environments.

papers.title: Age-dependent mechanical stress underlies unexpected vestibular differentiation and regeneration patterns

papers.title: Cell cycling throttles epithelial--mesenchymal transition

papers.title: Dynamic regulation of single-cell contractile heterogeneity in the human trabecular meshwork
papers.abstract: Altered trabecular meshwork (TM) mechanics contribute to increased aqueous humor outflow resistance and elevated intraocular pressure in glaucoma, yet how contractility is regulated across individual TM cells remains poorly understood. This response was progressively constrained as ECM stiffness increased and was absent on pathologically stiff substrates, demonstrating that extracellular mechanical context conditions glucocorticoid responsiveness. Finally, intracellular protein abundance poorly predicted functional mechanical behavior, with weak pooled associations reflecting divergent donor-specific relationships rather than consistent molecular-mechanical coupling. Together, these findings show that TM contractility emerges from integrating intrinsic cellular state and the extracellular mechanical environment rather than from either alone. More broadly, they identify single-cell contractile state as a functional dimension of TM cell identity that cannot be inferred from static molecular marker abundance or population-averaged mechanical measurements.

papers.title: Agile manufacturing of PDMS microfluidic devices for cell culture without a clean room

papers.title: Flagellotropic bacteriophage selects for evolutionary remodeling of cell motility and chemotaxis in Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Bacteria can evolve resistance to bacteriophage attack via mutations that alter phage receptors on the cell surface. papers.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans-QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. papers.title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell perturbation data by optimizing causal reach of latent mediator dynamics
papers.abstract: Resolving the causal structure of gene regulatory networks is central to understanding cellular regulation. Pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA readouts measure the transcriptional consequences of many interventions in parallel, providing a powerful resource for causal discovery. Combinatorial designs that perturb multiple regulators per cell increase throughput and can reveal responses that single-gene perturbations do not. However, inferring causal gene networks from these experiments remains challenging because gene regulatory interactions are nonlinear, dynamic, and often involve feedback. Thus, attributing the combined effect of several perturbations to individual regulators remains difficult. Additionally, transcriptional regulation is ultimately carried out by proteins, while single-cell perturbation datasets generally measure only RNA levels. Existing methods often simplify regulatory dynamics or rely on assumptions that conflict with gene regulation, such as acyclicity. Moreover, current evaluation practices usually rely on expression prediction error, which is readily computable in real datasets, but does not necessarily reflect graph quality. A complementary metric is needed to assess inferred regulatory connections using observed perturbation responses in real data. To address these challenges, we present CausalODE, a differentiable framework for learning causal graphs from single-cell perturbation data. Our approach incorporates three central insights to improve upon previous methods. First, genes that are differentially expressed when a gene is perturbed should be downstream of the target gene in the regulatory network; we quantify this property with a metric we term causal reach. Second, causal interactions involve transient cellular responses in RNA transcription, splicing, and degradation. Third, gene regulatory interactions are mediated by proteins, whose levels are not directly measured in single-cell RNA-seq experiments. Building on these insights, CausalODE learns a graph that optimizes the causal reach metric, captures transient cellular responses to perturbation, and explicitly models the latent dynamics of protein levels. Together, these components allow nonlinear responses, feedback loops, and time-lagged regulation. papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Osseointegration Using Titanium Implants Coated with Graphene and Niobium: An Animal Model Study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSurface modification may influence tissue-implant interactions. This exploratory study compared the biomechanical, coating-integrity, and histological responses associated with uncoated titanium and carbon- or niobium-containing surface-processing conditions in a rabbit model.MethodsTwelve adult male New Zealand White rabbits were initially enrolled and allocated to 30- and 60-day healing periods. Two animals were lost before endpoint and were not replaced; ten rabbits completed the study and were analyzed, with five animals at each period. Each rabbit received four implant-site conditions: uncoated titanium, carbon-based diamond-like carbon (Graphene-DLC), niobium deposited by chemical vapor deposition (Nb-CVD), and niobium deposited by sol-gel processing (Nb-Gel). Implant stability was assessed using reverse-torque testing after formalin fixation. Histological evaluation included hematoxylin and eosin and Picrosirius Red staining.ResultsAt 60 days, the uncoated titanium and Graphene-DLC conditions showed the highest reported mean reverse-torque values, whereas some niobium-containing conditions showed lower reported coating-integrity scores. Ordinal histological outcomes were interpreted descriptively because the sample was small, implant sites were clustered within rabbits, and implant condition was fixed to anatomical site.ConclusionsUnder this protocol, the observed differences describe combined implant-site conditions and do not provide unbiased causal evidence of coating-specific effects. The findings are exploratory and support further studies using randomized or counterbalanced allocation, clustered analysis, and independent biomechanical and histological specimens.

papers.title: Single Versus Double Implants in a Narrowed Mandibular Molar Space: A Finite Element Analysis.
papers.abstract: After molar loss, tipping of the adjacent teeth and extrusion of the opposing tooth often leave a mesiodistal space too narrow for a conventional implant. This study compared stress in the implant components and peri-implant bone among single- and double-implant configurations of different diameters in such a space. A mandibular model was constructed by computer-aided design; ridge resorption and mesial tipping of the second molar left a 13.6 mm mesiodistal space and a 7.5 mm crestal ridge width. Four configurations were modeled: 4.8 mm single (M1), 4.1 mm single (M2), 3.3 + 3.3 mm double (M3), and 4.1 + 3.3 mm double (M4). Vertical (150 N) and oblique (300 N at 45°) loads were applied; von Mises stress in the components and maximum and minimum principal stresses in bone were recorded. Oblique loading raised stress in every structure; because the oblique load was twice the vertical load, part of this increase reflects the higher force rather than loading direction alone, and direction-related increases (normalized per unit load) ranged from approximately 2- to 9-fold across components and bone. Under vertical loading, M1 gave the lowest implant body, abutment, and screw stresses (31.0, 36.7, and 16.1 MPa). Under oblique loading, M4 lowered implant body and abutment stress, whereas M1 retained the lowest screw (192.0 MPa) and configuration-level bone stresses (31.2 and 7.2 MPa). Because screw preload was not modeled, screw-stress comparisons should be interpreted as relative mechanical demand rather than as predictors of loosening or fracture risk. No configuration minimized stress in every structure. Implant diameter, site, component, and loading condition should be weighed together.

papers.title: One-Year Outcomes of Chairside Fully Guided Versus Conventional Partially Guided Implant Placement With Transcrestal Sinus Augmentation: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThis study represents the 1-year follow-up of a previously reported randomized controlled trial comparing chairside fully guided (FG) flapless implant placement with conventional partially guided (PG) open-flap implant placement. We evaluated marginal bone level (MBL) change, peri-implant clinical outcomes, and associations between placement accuracy and MBL change.Materials and methodsThis study was a 1-year follow-up analysis of a previously reported randomized controlled trial. Fifty-six patients were randomized into the FG (n = 28) and PG (n = 28) groups. Radiographic MBL changes and peri-implant clinical indices were evaluated at baseline and 1-year post-loading. Deviations between the virtually planned and placed implants were quantified in three dimensions. Stepwise multiple linear regression analyses were performed to identify accuracy parameters associated with MBL changes.ResultsTwenty-one FG and 22 PG patients completed follow-up. Peri-implant clinical parameters were comparable between groups. In unadjusted analyses, the FG group showed more positive mesial and mean ΔMBL values than the PG group. However, the treatment group was not significantly associated with mesial, distal, or mean ΔMBL in the adjusted models. Implant accuracy was higher in the FG group, with lower horizontal, three-dimensional, and angular deviations. Adjusted regression analyses retained TPD and distal EA in the mesial ΔMBL model and VAD in the mean ΔMBL model.ConclusionsChairside, FG flapless implant placement improved positional accuracy and was associated with modest unadjusted differences in short-term marginal bone level changes after crestal sinus augmentation. However, the between-group differences in ΔMBL were not statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons.Trial registrationClinical Research Information Service of the National Research Institute of Health, South Korea (KCT0005465), Registered October 12, 2020. https://cris.nih.go.kr/cris/search/detailSearch.do?seq=26961&search_page=L.

papers.title: Masseter Muscle Volume and Cross-Sectional Area as Risk Factors for Late Mechanical Dental Implant Failure: A Matched Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThis study aimed to investigate whether three-dimensional (3D) masseter muscle morphology-volume and cross-sectional area (CSA)-is associated with the risk of late mechanical dental implant failure and to derive preliminary cut-off values for risk stratification.Material and methodsThis 1:4 matched case-control study investigated 23 cases of late mechanical failure (fixture fracture, screw fracture, or abutment fracture) and 92 successful controls. Participants were matched by gender, age (±10 years), anatomical location, and maintenance period (±2 years). Masseter morphology was quantified using the 3D reconstruction of the cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) data. Independent risk factors were determined using a multivariable generalized estimating equation model adjusting for potential confounders.ResultsIncreased masseter muscle bulk was significantly associated with mechanical failure (p 3 increase in masseter volume and by 1.11-fold per 10 mm2 increase in CSA. ROC analysis demonstrated AUCs of 0.846 for masseter volume and 0.871 for CSA. The maximum-Youden thresholds were 31,272.56 mm3 for volume and 691.30 mm2 for CSA, with sensitivities of 86.96% and 82.61% and specificities of 77.17% and 79.35%, respectively. Internal bootstrap validation yielded AUC 95% confidence intervals of 0.751-0.931 and 0.767-0.951, respectively.ConclusionsGreater masseter muscle volume and CSA were significantly associated with late mechanical implant failure in this matched case-control study. The proposed cut-off values may provide preliminary reference values for risk stratification. However, these findings should be regarded as exploratory and require prospective validation in independent cohorts before routine clinical implementation.

papers.title: Association Between Local Factors and Implant-Related Complications: A Population-Sampled Cross-Sectional Analysis.
papers.abstract: AimTo investigate the role of local factors and the association with peri-implantitis and peri-implant soft-tissue dehiscence (PISTD).Materials and methodsA randomly selected sample of Norwegian patients who underwent implant therapy in 2014 was examined (242 patients; 732 implants). Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded, including soft-tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, connection type, platform switching, emergence angle, implant location and presence of adjacent teeth. To account for clustering of implants within patients, mixed-effects logistic regression models were applied.ResultsMucosal margin mobility, bone-level implants without platform switching, emergence angle > 45°, anterior implant location and daily smoking were identified as significant risk indicators for peri-implantitis. Thin soft-tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, absence of adjacent teeth, peri-implantitis and external connection were detected as significant indicators for PISTD. Peri-implantitis and PISTD were present in 8.7% and 25.0% of implants, respectively.ConclusionsLocal factors and soft-tissue-related parameters, many modifiable during treatment planning, were associated with peri-implantitis and PISTD. Particular attention should be given to soft-tissue phenotype, connection design, platform switching and prosthetic emergence angle. The relationship between systemic and local risk factors should be further investigated.

papers.title: Cilengitide limits syndromic and sporadic thoracic aortic aneurysm by targeting specific αV integrin.
papers.abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, still lacking an etiologic therapy. Aberrant activation of TGF-β and dysregulation of mechanotransduction signalling in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a key role in the pathology. However, a precise picture of molecular mechanisms in the disease is still unclear. Integrins containing the αV subunit are central in pro-fibrotic pathways mediated by TGF-β and mechanotransduction signalling pathways, but their role as a potential therapeutic target in syndromic and sporadic TAAs still needs investigation. We showed higher expression levels of αV integrin in both types of human TAAs and that the αV integrin inhibitor Cilengitide limits pro-fibrotic events in patient-derived VSMCs. In vivo results defined Cilengitide as the most effective and promising drug for the treatment of TAAs in humans.

papers.title: Source Geometry and Receiver Ascertainment Limit Spatial Perturbation Inference.
papers.abstract: Spatial perturbation assays locate targeted cells, but neighboring-cell responses can also reflect tissue structure, imperfect guide detection, and dependent sampling. We evaluated these alternatives with a spatial perturbation field diagnostic workflow combining independently specified receiver scores, spatial adjustment, and explicit source references. In 3 Spatial Perturb-Seq chips spanning 4 mice, a Clu-associated score was not exceptional under the stricter reference; training-only mouse holdouts also failed to establish stable program transfer. Known-effect injections showed that refitting spatial background retained 73.7% of the contrast gain at a 150-μm decay scale and 63.3% at 600 μm. In a separate count-level simulation, 3.82% receiver contamination by missed sources produced 33/100 zero-field rejections with source-autonomous expression changes, versus 3/100 without them. Perturb-map stromal contrasts were positive in 2 animals, but dependent sections, unresolved clone identities, and insufficient matched-placement support prevented population-level confirmation. External assays, injury, and clinical cohorts did not establish broad transportability or incremental prediction. These results distinguish limits in receiver ascertainment, source-reference validity, and biological replication, providing reproducible diagnostics rather than a generally calibrated test of causal propagation.

papers.title: Nano Particles, Big Impact: The Future of Regenerative Dentistry - A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: AimNanotechnology is emerging as a powerful tool in regenerative dentistry by supporting biological repair of enamel, dentin, pulp, periodontal tissues and alveolar bone. This narrative review outlines how nanotechnology provides a versatile platform for achieving regenerative dentistry by enabling targeted remineralization, controlled therapeutic delivery, and biomimetic tissue regeneration.MethodsThis review synthesizes current evidence from in vitro and in vivo studies, material science research, and recent reviews. Relevant literature was identified through electronic searches in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science up to February 2026, focusing on publications that investigate the mechanisms, efficacy, and applications of nanoparticles in regenerative dental therapies. Search terms included (nanoparticle OR nano OR nanomaterial) AND (regeneration OR regenerative OR remineralization OR mineralization) AND (enamel OR dentin OR pulp OR gingiva OR periodontal ligament OR cementum OR alveolar bone OR dental OR tooth OR oral).ResultsA total of 71 representative publications were selected. These studies focused on the use of nanoparticles for hard tissue remineralization, scaffold-enhanced regeneration, targeted drug delivery, and antimicrobial action in dental contexts. The findings indicate that nanoparticles promote hard tissue remineralization through calcium phosphate and hydroxyapatite systems that diffuse into subsurface lesions and nucleate new mineral formation. For alveolar bone regeneration, hydroxyapatite and bioactive glass nanoparticles provide osteoconductive scaffolds and osteoinductive ion signaling. In periodontal and pulp regeneration, nanoparticle-enhanced scaffolds support stem cell proliferation and differentiation through controlled growth factor delivery. Antimicrobial nanoparticles, particularly silver and zinc oxide, provide multi-target biofilm disruption with reduced resistance risk. The evidence base is predominantly preclinical, and routine clinical application is not yet supported by available data.ConclusionNanoparticles support dental tissue regeneration through mechanisms such as controlled ion release, sustained growth factor delivery, and antimicrobial activity. Key challenges include ensuring long-term biocompatibility, controlling degradation and potential toxicity, and establishing clear regulatory pathways.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in odontology education.
papers.abstract: IntroductionArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in dental education as a tool to support teaching, learning, assessment, and clinical decision-making. This systematic review synthesized current evidence on the implementation and educational impact of AI technologies in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing dental education.MethodologyA PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted using Scopus, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Studies published between 2020 and 2025 evaluating AI applications in dental education were identified using predefined PICO criteria. Educational outcomes included knowledge acquisition, diagnostic accuracy, clinical reasoning, procedural skills, learner engagement, and perceptions of AI-assisted learning.ResultsThe included literature reflects an expansion from machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision systems primarily evaluated for diagnostic support toward generative AI platforms, including large language models and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Across the included studies, AI applications were frequently associated with favorable diagnostic and examination performance and, in selected educational contexts, with supportive findings related to clinical reasoning, technical competency, feedback, and self-directed learning. However, the evidence was predominantly based on technical performance assessments and observational or cross-sectional designs.DiscussionAI is increasingly being explored as a potential complementary educational resource, with applications including interactive tutoring, adaptive learning, and support for clinical reasoning. Nevertheless, heterogeneous methodologies and limited longitudinal evidence indicate the need for standardized educational evaluation and responsible curricular integration.ConclusionAI shows potential as a complementary resource in dental education. Its integration should remain pedagogically guided and ethically supervised while future research establishes its educational effectiveness through standardized and longitudinal evaluation.

papers.title: Prognostic significance of minor versus major extranodal extension in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Extranodal extension (ENE) is an established adverse prognostic factor in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC), but the clinical relevance of its extent remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the prognostic impact of quantitatively defined minor versus major ENE, with particular emphasis on the conventional 2-mm threshold. PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026. Studies of surgically treated OCSCC assessing pathological ENE extent and oncological outcomes were included. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp inference were performed when at least three compatible adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were available. Risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. Twenty-two reports representing 18 independent cohorts were included. Five studies contributed to the primary overall survival (OS) meta-analysis. Major ENE was associated with significantly worse OS than minor ENE (pooled HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10-3.66; I2 = 60.5%). Three studies contributed to the disease-free survival (DFS) meta-analysis, showing a concordant but imprecise association (pooled HR 2.16, 95% CI 0.44-10.66; I2 = 59.3%). Alternative thresholds and morphological classifications also generally suggested poorer outcomes with increasing ENE extent. ENE extent provides prognostic information beyond binary ENE status in OCSCC. Major ENE is associated with worse OS, while evidence for DFS is directionally consistent but less precise. The 2-mm cutoff should be considered clinically useful but not yet biologically definitive.

papers.title: Temporomandibular joint arthrocentesis with viscosupplementation in patients with osteoarthritis: a retrospective analysis of the effect of the number of sessions.
papers.abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by pain, functional limitation, and reduced mouth opening. Arthrocentesis with hyaluronic acid (HA) viscosupplementation is a widely used minimally invasive treatment, often delivered according to a five-session protocol, although the optimal number of sessions remains unclear. This retrospective longitudinal observational study aimed to analyze session-specific clinical changes to identify the number of sessions required to achieve clinically relevant improvement. A total of 101 adult patients with TMJ OA unresponsive to at least 6 months of conservative therapy were included. All participants underwent five weekly arthrocentesis sessions including intra-articular HA injections. Pain at rest and during chewing, chewing efficacy, perceived functional limitation, assisted and non-assisted maximum mouth opening were assessed at baseline, before each session, and at 3-month follow-up. All clinical variables significantly improved from baseline to follow-up (all P 0.05). Pain at rest improved after sessions 1, 2, 3, and 5, and equally pain during chewing improved after sessions 1, 2, 3, and 5. Chewing efficacy improved after sessions 2, 3, and 5; likewise perceived functional limitation improved after the same sessions (all P 0.05). These findings support more individualized protocols with fewer interventions.

papers.title: Population-Stratified Evidence for the Yamamoto (2002) ≤0.8 mm Buccal Marrow Space Threshold and Neurosensory Disturbance Risk After Bilateral Sagittal Split Osteotomy: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Yamamoto et al. (2002) proposed that a buccal marrow space of 0.8 mm or less on preoperative CT is associated with a higher risk of neurosensory disturbance (NSD) after bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO), based on a single 20-patient cohort. Whether this threshold reproduces across populations now represented in the CBCT/CT morphometry literature has not been systematically tested. 12 databases were searched without date or language restriction (PROSPERO: CRD420261437829). Eligible studies reported buccal marrow width, measured directly or derivable from measurements at the same site, and were divided into Tier 1 (linked to postoperative NSD) or Tier 2 (normative data only). Risk of bias (JBI checklist, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale) and certainty of evidence (GRADE) were assessed, and measurement compatibility was assessed against the reference method and between studies. 42 records from 37 independent populations in 12 countries were included (12 Tier 1, 30 Tier 2); nine of the 12 Tier 1 studies were Japanese. Seven Tier 1 studies supported the association, three reported it descriptively without testing it, and two found none; the largest (Watanabe et al. 2026; 463 patients) found canal-cortex contact independently associated with NSD (OR 4.96, 95% CI 2.41-10.06). Only four of 26 Tier 2 populations reported individual ranges, two of which straddled 0.8 mm. No study outside Yamamoto's cohort tested and confirmed 0.8 mm as a predictor of NSD, and studies deriving or applying their own cut-offs arrived at 1.0-1.5 mm. No two studies used a compatible measurement protocol, so no data were pooled, and certainty was Very Low. Reduced buccal marrow space was associated with postoperative NSD in most studies, but 0.8 mm is not validated as a population-invariant threshold.

papers.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sinus Lift Versus Piezoelectric Lift Via Lateral Approach: A randomized controlled clinical trial.
papers.abstract: To assess the effectiveness of hydraulic pressure sinus lift via lateral wall approach versus piezoelectric surgery in patients with deficient posterior maxilla. This study involved a randomized clinical trial of 20 participants with less than 6 mm of bone height in the posterior maxilla in need of Maxillary Sinus Floor Augmentation using the lateral window approach. Patients were randomly assigned to two groups; the HPLT Group included 10 patients who underwent hydraulic pressure for osteotomy preparation for the lateral sinus lifting technique, while the PSLT Group included 10 patients managed using piezoelectric surgery. Clinical and radiographic assessment of bone augmentation, as well as intraoperative biological complications and postoperative complications, were recorded. Both groups showed insignificant differences in the recorded procedural duration, intraoperative complications, and reported postoperative pain. The HPLT group reported a statistically significant increase in bone height, with a mean height gain of 6.81 ± 1.85. The PSLT group reported a mean height gain of 5.51 ± 0.90. The difference between the compared groups regarding the final gain in bone height was statistically insignificant (P=0.061). Both hydraulic pressure-assisted and piezoelectric lateral sinus floor elevation resulted in increased radiographic bone height at six months, without a statistically significant difference between groups. Although these findings support the feasibility of hydraulic pressure-assisted sinus augmentation, the limited sample size prevents definitive conclusions regarding its comparative effectiveness and safety.

papers.title: N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
papers.abstract: BackgroundBronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a prevalent chronic lung disease in preterm infants, characterized by arrested alveolarization. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and receptor signaling are critical for alveolarization and are strictly regulated by protein N-glycosylation. However, the specific role of the vital post-translational modification in BPD pathogenesis remains unexplored. The present research aims to delineate a N-glycoproteomic landscape and elucidate the glycosylation-associated pathogenic mechanisms in a murine BPD model.MethodsTo establish BPD models, newborn mice were exposed to continuous hyperoxia (85% O2) for 14 days. Lung developmental impairment was quantified using Radial Alveolar Count (RAC) and Mean Linear Intercept (MLI). A comprehensive dual-omics profiling strategy was conducted, utilizing an Orbitrap Exploris 480 platform for global proteomics and a timsTOF Pro mass spectrometer for N-glycoproteomics. Key molecular targets were further validated by lectin histochemistry, Western blot, and AlphaFold-based spatial structure modeling.ResultsHyperoxia exposure successfully induced BPD-like lung injury, substantiated by a marked decline in RAC coupled with a concurrent elevation in MLI (P ConclusionThis study provides the first exhaustive N-glycoproteomic map of hyperoxia-induced BPD. Our results highlight dysregulated N-glycosylation, particularly the site-specific hypo-glycosylation of ITGB1 at Asn212. Based on computational predictions, it is hypothesized to severely disrupts the ECM-receptor networks and integrin affinity, which correlates with potentially driving alveolarization arrest. These insights provide a novel post-translational perspective on BPD pathogenesis and offer new avenues for future investigation into potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: KOS® Implants: A Case of Full Mouth Rehabilitation in One Day.
papers.abstract: Full-mouth rehabilitation in edentulous patients remains a clinical challenge, particularly when bone resorption and prosthetic instability are present. This report discusses the case of a 56-year-old female patient with long-term edentulism and compromised removable prostheses who underwent extraction of the remaining anterior lower teeth and immediate placement of 22 single-piece compressive KOS® (Dr. Ihde Dental AG, Gommiswald, CHE) and basal cortical screw (BCS®; Dr. Ihde Dental AG) implants using a flapless approach. Within the same day, provisional polymethyl methacrylate bridges were delivered, restoring occlusion, aesthetics, and facial support. The patient reported superior comfort and stability compared to her previous removable prostheses. Immediate loading with compressive and basal implants provided predictable stability and rapid functional and aesthetic improvement, demonstrating the efficiency of modern implantology in complex edentulous cases.

papers.title: Dual-action nanotheranostics targeting cell-free DNA rescues aberrant alternative polyadenylation to ameliorate periodontitis.
papers.abstract: While periodontal pathogens (Porphyromonas gingivalis) are known to severely disrupt macrophage post-transcriptional homeostasis, the precise extracellular instigator remains elusive. Here, through comparative transcriptomic profiling, we identify cell-free DNA (cfDNA) as this fundamental pathogenic trigger. Comprehensive bioinformatic analysis uncovers that cfDNA governs macrophage fate by fundamentally rewiring the global alternative polyadenylation (APA) equilibrium. Specifically, cfDNA forces pro-inflammatory (M1) transcripts into translationally hyperactive short-3'-untranslated region (3'UTR) isoforms, while simultaneously suppressing anti-inflammatory (M2) programs via 3'UTR lengthening. To therapeutically intercept this cfDNA-APA pathogenic axis, we engineered a homologous nanotheranostic platform (DA-APAT). Addressing the unique clinical demands for early periodontitis screening, its polycationic PEI shell enables highly sensitive salivary cfDNA theranostic monitoring. Crucially, this monitoring readout directly calibrates the in situ enzymatic clearance load executed by the internally encapsulated DNase I. Synergized by the intrinsic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capability of the hollow mesoporous cerium oxide core, this monitoring nanoplatform decisively silences intracellular DNA-sensing pathways (cGAS-STING/TLR9), rectifies the disrupted APA, and contributes robust M2 macrophage repolarization. In an orthotopic murine periodontitis model, this nanotherapy effectively halts alveolar bone loss and facilitates profound periodontal regeneration with excellent biocompatibility. This work unveils a cfDNA-driven RNA regulatory paradigm in immune dysregulation and provides a monitoring precision nanotheranostic modality for inflammatory therapy.

papers.abstract: BackgroundAlveolar bone loss following tooth extraction remains a major clinical concern that may compromise future implant placement and prosthetic rehabilitation. Histological evaluation was performed using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Masson's trichrome staining. Histomorphometric analysis quantified the percentage of newly formed bone area within standardized regions of interest using calibrated ImageJ software. Differences among treatment groups were analyzed separately at each healing interval using one-way ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test, as appropriate, followed by appropriate post-hoc multiple comparisons. Statistical significance was set at p ResultsBoth HA-treated groups demonstrated significantly greater bone formation compared with extraction alone at all healing intervals (p 0.05).ConclusionWithin the limitations of this exploratory pilot animal study, HA significantly enhanced extraction socket healing by promoting new bone formation, improving trabecular organization, and increasing collagen deposition compared with spontaneous healing.
