papers.title: Microenvironmental Perfusion Gradients Shape the CpG Methylome to Drive Glioblastoma Intratumoral Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits intense intratumoral heterogeneity, primarily driven by abnormal vasculature that establishes distinct perfusion and oxygen gradients. Although these perfusion-defined niches possess unique transcriptomic and metabolic signatures, the upstream hierarchical drivers of these variations remain unresolved. Here, we combined Perfusion-based Fluorescent Dye Labeling of Cells (PFDLC) with high-density methylation profiling microarray to evaluate how regional perfusion variations shape niche-specific CpG methylation landscapes in GBM cells. We isolated perivascular, intermediate, and hypoxic cancer cell subpopulations based on their proximity to functional blood vessels. Pan-genomic profiling revealed that the most extensive CpG methylation variations occur at the microenvironmental extremes, closely tracking the tumor's perfusion gradient. These altered sites target transcriptionally critical promoter regions and CpG islands linked to separate, complementary oncogenic cascades. Multi-omic integration of our niche-specific methylome and transcriptome datasets revealed that promoter hypomethylation exercises a dominant role over hypermethylation in driving active transcription. Integrating these methylomic signatures with niche-specific transcriptomes identified a core set of hypoxia-regulated genes — ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1), Glycogen branching enzyme 1 (GBE1), Glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B (GPNMB) and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 14 (CXCL14) — where hypomethylation correlates with transcriptional upregulation. Elevated expression of these candidates clinically associates with highly aggressive tumor phenotypes, therapy resistance, and reduced patient survival. Multi-modal cross-species validations across tumor xenografts, patient tissue immunohistochemistry, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics confirmed the robust enrichment of these malignant targets within perfusion-deprived hypoxic microdomains. Collectively, these findings define a perfusion-methylome-transcriptome axis that reproducibly marks the most aggressive, treatment-refractory compartment of GBM, nominating ABCA1, GBE1, and GPNMB as candidate biomarkers for hypoxia-informed patient stratification and epigenetically directed precision therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: A Single-Cell Atlas of PVOD Across the Lifespan Reveals Cellular and Molecular Therapeutic Targets
papers.abstract: Rationale Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD) is a progressive and lethal disease cured only lung transplant. While genetic mutations in EIF2AK4 have been identified in some cases, 70% of PVOD patients have no known etiology. Objectives To construct a single-cell atlas to define the cellular and molecular constituents driving pathophysiology in PVOD. Methods Lung samples were collected from four idiopathic non- EIF2AK4 mutation pediatric and adult PVOD patients and age-matched controls. Analyses of single-cell RNA sequencing, Xenium spatial transcriptomics, and immunohistochemistry were performed to identify cell state changes and differential gene expression between controls and PVOD and subsequent transcriptome comparison between our PVOD and published pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) datasets. Measurement and Main Results The single-cell atlas reveals marked changes in the PVOD endothelium compared to controls. EndMT and ectopic COL15A1+ systemic venous shunts and pulmonary vein endothelium are hallmarks of PVOD. Molecular analyses reveal activation of the integrated stress response (ISR)/ATF4, TGFβ signaling, MAPK signaling, and BRD4 are potential key players in the pathophysiology of PVOD. While PVOD and PAH share both pathological and some molecular mechanisms, ISR and TGFβ signaling are more prominent in PVOD than PAH. Conclusions These data indicate that endothelial dysfunction is a primary etiology in the development of PVOD with activation of multiple pathways with druggable targets. At a Glance Commentary Scientific Knowledge of the Subject Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD) is driven by progressive vasculopathy of the pulmonary veins and capillaries that results in significant pre-lung transplant mortality. Only 30% of PVOD cases can be explained by genetic mutations in EIF2AK4 , a critical protein translation factor associated with the integrated stress response. Thus, the majority of PVOD cases have no known molecular and cellular etiologies. What This Study Adds to the Field This study generated a cell atlas of idiopathic PVOD in patients with the more common, non- EIF2AK4 mutation etiology. This cell atlas defines pathological cell state changes in the lung vasculature including aberrant populations in the endothelium of veins and capillaries. These data also provide key insight into the molecular underpinnings driving PVOD disease and identified both novel and common targetable pulmonary vascular disease pathways with known drugs that are currently under investigation or FDA approved.

papers.title: Lack of adoption of computational gene-panel-selection tools in targeted spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Targeted spatial transcriptomics requires selecting a gene panel before any experiment is run. Choosing well across tens of thousands of candidate genes under platform-specific probe, panelsize, and sensitivity constraints is difficult to do manually, and impossible to correct once a panel has been used. A growing number of computational tools to automate this selection have been designed, yet it remains unclear whether they are adopted in practice. Several factors could limit uptake: validation uncertainty about panel performance, workflow friction between a ranked gene list and a submission-ready panel, limited platform awareness in tools developed for dissociated single-cell data, and the cost advantage of vendor panels. We analyzed 18 computational tools for gene-panel selection from two angles: their citation landscape and their use across a targeted spatial transcriptomics corpus. Across 540 full-text-classified records, only 35 (6.5%) reported using the cited tool for panel design; most came from computational, benchmark, review, or non-spatial papers, or papers that cited but did not use it. In an independent corpus, only 34 of 479 (7.1%) involved a computational tool, alone or in a hybrid workflow; most used manually curated, premade vendor, or modified vendor panels. Both lines of evidence point the same way: computational selection is rarely part of the reported experimental workflow, and it more often supplemented manual curation than replaced it. Adoption is unlikely to turn on further benchmark gains alone; it will depend on reducing the validation uncertainty and workflow friction that keep users on established panel-design practice.

papers.title: Dysregulation of epithelial differentiation architecture underlies field cancerization in head and neck cancer
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) has exceptionally high recurrence rates, exceeding 50%, contributing to mortality and morbidity. This recurrence rate is proposed to be due to field cancerization, a phenomenon where tumor-adjacent “field” tissue that appears histologically normal harbors molecular changes that prime it for subsequent tumor growth. Current models attribute field cancerization to shared driver mutations between tumors and adjacent at-risk tissue, but this assumption has never been directly tested. To comprehensively characterize this phenomenon, we profiled patient-matched tumor, normal-adjacent field (NAF), contralateral normal, and blood samples from HPV-negative HNSCC patients using whole genome sequencing, targeted driver gene sequencing, single-nucleus multiome profiling, spatial transcriptomics and functional proliferation assays. While histologically normal NAF tissues did harbor expanded mutant clones, these mutations rarely overlapped with paired tumors and were not shared across patients, suggesting molecular features beyond mutations are altered in NAF. Single-cell multiomics revealed that NAF epithelium loses its normal organizational hierarchy: basal stem cell markers persist in differentiated cells, while terminal differentiation programs fail to activate, with reconfiguration of both gene regulatory networks and cell-cell interactions. Proliferating cells appeared in tissue layers normally restricted to post-mitotic cells, a pattern typically seen only in overt dysplasia. Within this disrupted hierarchy, a distinct epithelial state arose in NAF that expressed both normal epithelial and tumor-associated markers, which we localized to the parabasal layers using immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics. Together, our findings demonstrate that field cancerization operates through epithelial hierarchy disorganization that disrupts differentiation, generates cells with tumor-like features, and may create a permissive environment for the expansion of cancer-associated mutations, all within tissue that appears histologically normal.

papers.title: Stress Distribution in Short Zirconia and Titanium Dental Implants: A Finite Element Study
papers.abstract: Treatment with short implants is considered as predictable as conventional implants. Objective: This in silico experimental study aimed to determine the stress distribution in short zirconia dental implants using finite element analysis (FEA). Methods: Thirty-six implant-crown designs were modeled in ANSYS 2019 R2. Loading conditions included an oblique force of 150 N (30°, ISO 14801:2016), vertical forces of 300 N and 400 N, and a 32 Ncm screw tightening torque across Type I and Type III bone models using three implant diameters (4.1, 4.8, and 5.0 mm). Results: Under both oblique and vertical loads, zirconia generated lower bone deformation but higher overall stress concentrations than titanium. When stratified by bone density, zirconia concentrated higher peri-implant stress in low-density (Type III) bone. Discussion: In both loading scenarios, a progressive increase in implant diameter successfully and proportionally mitigated stress concentrations, which aligns with established biomechanical literature on titanium systems while matching findings from recent comparative studies showing elevated stress levels in zirconia structures. Conclusion: Stress concentrations are higher in zirconia than titanium, particularly in low-density bone; however, this biomechanical limitation can be effectively compensated for by increasing the implant diameter.

papers.title: Multi-Target Anti-Aging and Wound-Healing Potential of Libyan Thymus vulgaris and Thymus capitatus Essential Oils: Integrated GC-MS, Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Thymus vulgaris (TV) and Thymus capitatus (TC) are traditionally used for skin-related disorders, but their comparative chemical composition and multi-target skin-protective mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized. GC-MS identified 39 constituents, accounting for 98.95% and 99.23% of the TV and TC oils, respectively; carvacrol (41.38%) and thymol (20.91%) predominated in TV, whereas thymol (41.06%) and carvacrol (13.02%) predominated in TC. Chemometric comparison with 28 published oils per species (PCA and hierarchical clustering) classified the TC oil as a thymol chemotype, found in only seven of 28 regional T. capitatus oils (18 were carvacrol type), and the TV oil as a carvacrol-rich type most similar to Moroccan oils. Network pharmacology identified 1074 core targets linked to 14 skin-associated conditions and prioritised 50 hub genes, including NFKB1 and RELA. Docking of 129 compound-target pairs showed that 84 (65%) achieved docking scores ≤-5.0 kcal/mol. TC showed stronger elastase, tyrosinase, hyaluronidase, and 5-LOX inhibition, whereas TV exhibited stronger COX-2 inhibition and antioxidant activity. At a low-toxicity concentration (1.99 µg/mL), TC was associated with accelerated fibroblast wound closure, which may reflect both migration and proliferation, and with increased COL1A1, ITGA11, and HAS2 and decreased MMP1 mRNA expression. Overall, the two oils displayed complementary multi-target anti-aging, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities in vitro and in silico, with TC additionally suggesting pro-regenerative potential in fibroblasts, supporting their further investigation as topical cosmeceutical candidates.

papers.title: Extracellular Vesicles in Breast Cancer: Immunomodulation, Biomarkers, and Therapy.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are key mediators of intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment (TME). In this narrative review, we synthesized relevant studies identified through a systematic search of PubMed and Web of Science (2020-2026), using search terms including "EVs", "breast cancer", "tumor microenvironment", "biomarkers", "macrophages", "fibroblasts", "T cells", and "therapy". Priority was given to peer-reviewed original research and recent high-quality reviews, with study selection based on relevance to EV biology, clinical translation, and methodological rigor. We first outline the potential roles of EVs in breast cancer pathogenesis, including their contribution to an immunosuppressive microenvironment, their regulatory effects on neighboring cells within the TME, and their promotion of malignant phenotypes in epithelial and vascular endothelial cells. Next, we outline studies on EV-based applications for early detection and prognostic stratification. Finally, we introduce emerging EV-related therapeutic strategies-such as adjuvant immunotherapy, stem cell-derived EVs, and engineered EVs-which remain primarily preclinical and face challenges including the lack of standardized isolation and characterization protocols, as well as unresolved issues regarding dosing, safety, and production. EVs are not yet established therapeutic tools; rather, they represent promising but unproven candidate therapies, with most clinical studies focusing on diagnostic applications. Through a narrative and critical review of the relevant literature, this review aims to advance the translation of EV research into more rigorous and practical applications for breast cancer diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Integrative genomics and experimental validation identify a mechanosensitive gene signature associated with colorectal cancer liver metastasis.
papers.abstract: The mechanical tumor microenvironment critically influences colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis, yet the underlying molecular mediators remain poorly defined. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics, bulk RNA-seq, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and 117 machine learning algorithms, we identified a six-gene mechanosensitive signature (SNX7, SDC1, CDCP1, PTGES, EMP2, and CALB2) associated with CRC liver metastasis. This signature demonstrated superior prognostic performance (mean C-index 0.68) across multiple independent cohorts compared to 74 published CRC signatures. Among these genes, SDC1 was consistently upregulated in CRC cells and tissues, and its expression was further induced by increased matrix stiffness in tunable hydrogel culture systems. These findings support a mechanosensitive gene signature with robust prognostic value and identify SDC1 as a stiffness-responsive candidate regulator, providing insights into the mechanobiological regulation of CRC metastasis.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omic Analysis of Paired Primary and Peritoneal Metastatic Tumors Reveals GPAA1 as a Therapeutic Target in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis confers a dismal prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC-PM), with median survival rarely exceeding 20 months. Here we employed multi-omic profiling to identify actionable drivers of CRC-PM. We performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) and label-free quantitative proteomics on 13 and 7 matched primary-peritoneal metastasis pairs, respectively. Public single-cell (GSE183916 and GSE132465) and spatial transcriptomic datasets (GSE225857) were integrated to dissect cellular heterogeneity. TCGA cohorts were used for survival analysis, and functional validation was performed in DLD1 cells. GPAA1, a catalytic subunit of the GPI transamidase complex, emerged as the most consistently upregulated protein in peritoneal metastases across discovery and validation proteomic cohorts. High GPAA1 expression correlated with shorter recurrence-free survival (HR = 1.72, p = 3.4 × 10-5). Single-cell analysis localized GPAA1 to malignant cells exhibiting oxidative phosphorylation and enhanced stromal crosstalk. GPAA1 overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, and EMT via AKT activation, whereas knockdown reversed these phenotypes. Our findings identify GPAA1 as a candidate driver of peritoneal metastasis in CRC, linking GPI anchor biosynthesis to metabolic reprogramming and AKT-mediated EMT. Soft-tissue recession, dehiscence, mucositis, and framework exposure are the dominant biological complications and appear central to late failure. Applications are expanding beyond full-arch atrophic jaws to sectional, congenital, salvage, and oncologic reconstruction despite marked heterogeneity in indications, device design, loading protocols, and outcome definitions. papers.title: Adjunctive Strategies to Enhance Antimicrobial Photodynamic Therapy in Oral Infections: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) is a widely investigated adjunct for managing oral biofilm-associated bacterial and fungal infections, but poor photosensitizer penetration, aggregation, biofilm hypoxia, and protocol variability limit its clinical efficacy. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched for English-language RCTs. Eligible studies evaluated aPDT combined with physicochemical, delivery-based, light-based, biological, or host-modulating adjuncts in patients with oral biofilm-related bacterial or fungal disease, using an appropriate comparator. Data were synthesized narratively due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, and risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Results: Fourteen RCTs were included, predominantly addressing periodontal and peri-implant conditions, with additional studies involving orthodontic biofilms; no eligible RCT evaluated a fungal oral infection. Surfactant-based enhancement (e.g., sodium dodecyl sulfate) produced formulation- and protocol-dependent effects, with benefits reported for methylene blue and curcumin but not riboflavin. Nanocarrier-based photosensitizer delivery, evaluated in combination with Aloe vera vehicles, improved selected clinical outcomes without consistently superior microbiological effects; however, the independent contribution of the nanocarrier could not be isolated from the potential bioactive effects of the vehicle. An oxygen-releasing adjunct showed no significant between-group clinical benefit. Repeated dual-light irradiation improved bleeding on probing and pocket-related outcomes in some but not all trials. Probiotics, vitamin D, and low-level laser therapy showed inconsistent or preliminary benefits, each supported by limited trial numbers. Risk-of-bias assessments predominantly indicated low risk or some concerns, with one study judged at high overall risk. Conclusions: Enhancement of aPDT should not be regarded as a single therapeutic concept; its clinical benefit is strategy-, formulation-, and context-dependent. Current randomized evidence does not support a universally superior adjunct, highlighting the need for standardized, adequately powered trials with mechanism-oriented comparator designs.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in digital implant dentistry: current applications, clinical translation, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly expanded across digital implant dentistry, with applications ranging from diagnosis and treatment planning to surgical execution, prosthetic rehabilitation, outcome prediction, and biomechanical optimization. A comprehensive narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by Google Scholar and manual reference screening. The review was prepared according to SANRA recommendations. AI has demonstrated promising performance in automated image analysis, implant planning, computer-assisted surgery, prosthetic workflows, implant identification, peri-implant disease detection, predictive modelling, and biomechanical optimization. Nevertheless, most available evidence is derived from retrospective studies, simulation-based investigations, or single-center datasets. Limited external validation, heterogeneity in study design, and insufficient prospective clinical evidence continue to restrict widespread clinical adoption. Furthermore, improvements in technical performance do not necessarily translate into superior patient-centered outcomes. AI has the potential to enhance efficiency, consistency, and clinical decision support throughout the implant workflow. However, current evidence supports its role primarily as an adjunctive tool rather than an autonomous clinical system. Future progress will depend on robust validation, standardized reporting, explainable AI frameworks, and prospective clinical studies demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes. Clinical Relevance Statement: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in the digital implant workflow, from radiographic analysis and virtual patient construction to computer-assisted surgery, prosthetic design, and outcome prediction. This review helps clinicians distinguish the AI-specific components of these technologies from conventional digital tools, identify which applications are supported by clinical evidence versus those that remain experimental, and understand the current limitations regarding validation, generalizability, and regulatory status. This knowledge supports informed adoption of AI as an adjunctive decision-support tool while maintaining clinician-led verification and patient-centered care.

papers.title: Adjunctive Antimicrobial Therapy in Peri-Implant Diseases: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Background: Effective management of peri-implant disease relies primarily on mechanical removal of the bacterial biofilm. However, achieving adequate surface decontamination can be challenging due to complex implant-surface morphology and restricted access to deep peri-implant pockets. This has prompted the use of adjunctive antimicrobial agents to complement mechanical therapy and improve therapeutic outcomes. Objective: To investigate whether the adjunctive use of antimicrobial strategies improves clinical, microbiological, and radiographic outcomes in patients with peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis. Materials and Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus in July 2026. No database filters concerning language, human participants or study design were applied. During the screening process, only randomized controlled clinical trials involving human participants and available as English-language full texts were selected. Eligible interventions included locally or systemically administered antibiotics, antiseptics, antimicrobial drug-delivery systems, antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT), ozone-based therapies, and microbiome-modulating adjuncts. Conventional laser therapy was not classified as an eligible antimicrobial intervention. The database searches retrieved 462 records, including 252 from PubMed and 210 from Scopus. Following duplicate removal and eligibility assessment, 100 publications representing 93 independent clinical trials were included. Results: adjunctive antimicrobial efficacy was highly variable and appeared to depend on disease severity, debridement strategy, antimicrobial agent, delivery modality, and follow-up period. Repeated or sustained local antimicrobial delivery was associated with modest, short-term benefits in several studies, whereas chlorhexidine (CHX) generally provided limited additional benefit over mechanical therapy. Evidence for systemic antibiotics remained inconsistent and insufficient to support routine use, while aPDT offered potential benefits that varied according to treatment protocol. Ozone therapy, herbal agents, and novel drug-delivery systems yielded encouraging preliminary results, although evidence remains scarce. Moreover, reductions in bleeding and probing depth (PD) did not reliably correspond to superior microbiological outcomes, radiographic bone gain, or complete disease resolution. Conclusions: Mechanical debridement (MD) and effective plaque control remain central to peri-implant disease management. Some adjunctive interventions produced modest short-term improvements in individual studies; however, the available evidence does not demonstrate durable disease control or support routine use. Therapeutic decisions should be tailored to disease severity, patient and implant characteristics, and the balance between potential benefits and antimicrobial-associated risks. Further well-designed and adequately powered randomized controlled trials with extended follow-up periods are needed to establish more definitive recommendations.

papers.title: Advances in Single-Cell and Spatial Omics for Glioblastoma Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: Purpose of reviewGlioblastoma is the most aggressive and fatal primary malignant brain tumour in adults, characterised by extensive intra-tumour heterogeneity, diffuse infiltration into surrounding brain tissue. Despite advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, patient prognosis remains poor, underscoring the critical need for improved biological insight to guide precision medicine potential strategies. Although traditional bulk genomic and transcriptomic analyses have made a substantial contribution to understanding glioblastoma pathophysiology, such average molecular signals across cell populations obscures tumour microenvironment influence and clinically significant cellular states.Recent findingsRecent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies have revolutionised glioblastoma research by enabling high-resolution analysis of tumour composition, cellular plasticity, and spatial organisation. These modalities have revealed that glioblastoma is composed of dynamic and plastic cellular states as opposed to fixed molecular subtypes, including stem-like and therapy-resistant populations that contribute to recurrence. The tumour architecture is preserved by spatially resolved transcriptomic and proteomic approaches, which reveal regional transcriptional programmes influenced by the tumour ecosystem. The findings provide a more resolved view of glioblastoma evolution and treatment resistance, challenging current classification systems. However, significant challenges remain in integrating these high-dimensional datasets, managing technical and computational demands, and translating these approaches into clinically scalable workflows which collectively hinder their translational adoption. This review aims to synthesise recent advances in glioblastoma single-cell and spatial omics, critically evaluating both advantages and limitations in understanding tumour heterogeneity and tumour microenvironmental interactions. Furthermore, it assesses the current challenges of glioblastoma precision medicine and evaluates the potential of these technologies to advance such approaches.

papers.abstract: BackgroundDegenerative cervical radiculopathy (CR) causes neck and upper-extremity pain, sensory disturbance, and motor dysfunction resulting from nerve root compression or irritation by disc herniation, foraminal narrowing, or spondylotic changes. Ultrasound-guided acupotomy (UA), a minimally invasive acupuncture-based intervention, permits real-time visualization of target tissues and adjacent neurovascular structures, enabling controlled release of fibrotic or adhesive soft tissues that may contribute to nerve root compression. Evidence on its effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness remains limited.MethodsThis two-arm, parallel, single-center randomized controlled trial will enroll 56 patients with clinically and radiologically confirmed degenerative CR, randomized 1:1 to UA or conventional physical therapy (CPT; interferential current therapy and microwave diathermy). Both groups will receive six sessions over 3 weeks, with follow-up at weeks 4, 7, and 11. The primary outcome is the between-group difference in mean change from baseline in visual analog scale scores for cervical and/or upper-extremity pain/discomfort at week 4. Secondary outcomes include painDETECT, Neck Disability Index, EuroQol 5-dimension 5-level, Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21, Patient Global Impression of Change, clinically important difference, rescue medication use, Work Productivity and Activity Impairment, and cervical multifidus stiffness on shear wave elastography (SWE), interpreted as exploratory. Adverse events will be recorded at every visit.ConclusionThis trial will evaluate the effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness of UA versus CPT for degenerative CR. By integrating clinical outcomes, economic evaluation, magnetic resonance imaging-based foraminal stenosis grading, and exploratory SWE assessment, findings may provide comprehensive evidence on the role of UA in CR management.Ethics and disseminationThis protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Pusan National University Korean Medicine Hospital. Written informed consent will be obtained from each participant after the study aims, procedures, and potential risks have been explained.Trial registrationClinical Research Information Service, KCT0011139; registered on 12 November 2025.

papers.title: Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis of inflammation-metabolism programs and the tumor microenvironment of colorectal cancer liver metastasis.
papers.abstract: BackgroundColorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) is a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC) and develops within a heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME). How immune, stromal, and metabolic programs differ between primary CRC and matched liver metastases remains incompletely resolved.MethodsWe analyzed publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from GSE178318 (15 specimens from six patients: six primary CRC samples, six matched liver metastases, and three peripheral-blood mononuclear cell samples) together with bulk RNA-seq data from GSE50760 (54 samples from 18 patients spanning normal colon, primary CRC, and liver metastasis). The single-cell workflow included quality control, score-based cell-type annotation, patient-level pseudobulk differential expression, pathway/module scoring, ligand-receptor co-expression analysis, and diffusion-map pseudotime. Bulk data were assessed using within-patient paired comparisons, co-expression analysis, and program-level scoring. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied for multiple testing.ResultsAfter quality control, 132,915 single cells were retained. Liver metastases showed higher patient-level T/NK-cell fractions and lower malignant epithelial and B/plasma-cell fractions than primary tumors. In paired single-cell pseudobulk analysis, no gene remained significant at the prespecified FDR threshold, although nominal differences suggested extracellular-matrix and metabolic changes. Glycolysis scores were modestly higher and oxidative-phosphorylation scores modestly lower in liver metastases, whereas inflammatory and glycolytic scores were not correlated at the patient-tissue level. Ligand-receptor co-expression was strongest for MIF-CD74, VIM-CD44, and HLA-A-CD8A, with CAF/stromal and myeloid/TAM populations showing high aggregate outgoing scores. Diffusion pseudotime showed increasing EMT/invasion scores and decreasing glycolysis along the inferred transcriptomic ordering; this ordering is descriptive and not a longitudinal lineage. In the bulk cohort, 654 genes differed between liver metastasis and primary tumor, while cross-platform rank concordance was weak (Spearman rho=0.106).ConclusionsPublic single-cell and bulk datasets support compartment-associated differences in cellular composition and transcriptional programs in CRLM, with prominent stromal, myeloid, and metabolic features. However, limited patient numbers, cross-sectional sampling, weak cross-platform concordance, and the absence of experimental validation mean that the ligand-receptor and trajectory findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal or clinically validated.

papers.title: Disentangled Information Asymmetry in Spatial High-dimensional Data Interpretation.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in sensor technology have led to an explosion of Spatial High-Dimensional Data (SHD), including spatial transcriptomics and hyperspectral imaging, the two domains studied in this work. These data capture complex interactions between intrinsic sample properties and spatial microenvironments by incorporating location information through accumulation, embedding, or aggregation. Existing methods typically assume homogeneous spatial interaction patterns, overlooking critical asymmetries in SHD: (i) view asymmetry between spatial patterns and high-dimensional attributes, and (ii) spatial asymmetry in the internal pathways of high-dimensional data. To address this gap, we propose DIaS, a data-centric decoupling framework that disentangles spatial-induced, intrinsic, and harmonized information signals to better model the richness of SHD. Specifically, DIaS employs a Gaussian process for spatial embedding, leveraging uncertainty quantification to dynamically infer spatial pathways. During disentanglement, SHD is decomposed into three mutually regularized views to minimize dependence between spatial attributes and intrinsic features. To balance the asymmetric contributions of spatial and intrinsic information, we introduce an asymmetric harmonization mechanism, which adaptively aligns spatial and intrinsic representations to identify salient and diverse multi-view prototypes. Experiments on 18 benchmarks in spatial transcriptomics and hyperspectral imaging, together with downstream task evaluations, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and the effectiveness of DIaS in alleviating information asymmetry within these two domains. The demo code of this work is publicly available at https://github.com/hexiao0275/DIaS.

papers.title: Standardized Clinical Photography for Improving Dermatological Treatment Adherence (Scoping Review): Evidence Landscape and Research Gaps.
papers.abstract: Treatment adherence remains suboptimal across chronic dermatological conditions, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and increased healthcare burden. Despite the established role of standardized clinical photography in clinical documentation, its specific application as an adherence-promoting intervention remains poorly characterized. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the literature on photographic feedback in dermatology, identify research gaps, and propose methodological recommendations for future randomized controlled trials (RCTs). We conducted a scoping review according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Systematic searches of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science, supplemented by Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, and Google Scholar (first 200 records), were performed from database inception to December 31, 2025 (searches executed September 20-27, 2026). Of 1181 identified records, 18 studies met the eligibility criteria: five provided direct evidence, five indirect evidence, and eight methodological evidence. Direct evidence comprised three observational studies in hair loss disorders encompassing 3,218 patients (93% of participants derived from a single retrospective cohort), one virtual feasibility study in atopic dermatitis, and one remote photographic wound-monitoring study in keloids; the remaining five prespecified conditions (psoriasis, acne, vitiligo, rosacea, and melasma) yielded zero direct evidence, although vitiligo has an established methodological photography literature. Of the five direct-evidence studies, four measured motivation, satisfaction, task completion, or image-upload compliance rather than treatment adherence per se. Indirect evidence from smartphone applications exists for psoriasis and atopic dermatitis, but these bundle photography with other digital functions. We propose the "early difference refutation" design to address reverse causality in future RCTs. High-quality RCTs are urgently needed to determine whether photographic feedback alone can improve dermatological treatment adherence.

papers.title: Accuracy of transfer learning in predicting peri-implantitis onset from intraoral radiograph: A multi-center longitudinal retrospective study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe growing application of artificial intelligence in dentistry has opened new opportunities for predicting peri-implantitis (PI) using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Transfer learning, where knowledge from a model pre-trained on a large dataset is adapted to a new, domain-specific task, may enhance performance, particularly when medical datasets are limited. This study evaluated the ability of several pre-trained CNN architectures applied to baseline 2D intraoral radiographs to predict peri-implantitis onset.MethodsA retrospective multi-center study was conducted at the University of Michigan and King's College London. A total of 195 implants (146 from Michigan and 49 from London) placed in 108 maintained patients were included. For each implant, a baseline periapical radiograph taken up to one year after prosthetic restoration was analyzed. Five pre-trained CNN architectures (ResNet50, DenseNet, VGG16, InceptionV3, EfficientNet) were combined with four transfer learning strategies: feature extraction (hybrid and non-hybrid), partial fine-tuning (50% of layers), and full fine-tuning. Models were trained using patient-wise splits to avoid leakage, and performance was evaluated on an independent test set using accuracy, area under the ROC curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity.ResultsAll CNN architectures showed variable performance across transfer learning strategies. The non-hybrid feature extraction approach provided the most consistent discrimination, with the best models achieving AUC values between 0.74 and 0.83. InceptionV3 reached the highest AUC (0.83). Fine-tuning strategies yielded modest or low performance, with AUCs generally ranging from 0.42 to 0.69 across architectures.ConclusionNon-hybrid feature extraction applied to pre-trained CNNs showed the most promising, though moderate, performance for predicting PI onset from baseline intraoral radiographs. These findings indicate that transfer learning may assist early risk stratification in implant dentistry, but larger prospective studies are needed before clinical adoption.Clinical relevanceDeep learning models may serve as adjunctive tools to identify implants at higher risk for future PI based on routine baseline radiographs, supporting more individualized maintenance protocols and earlier preventive interventions.

papers.title: Minimally invasive implant-assisted removable partial dentures with surveyed crowns for atrophic edentulous arches: a retrospective case series with up to a 67-month follow-up.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe rehabilitation of completely edentulous arches with fixed implant-supported prostheses is often precluded by systemic, anatomic, or financial constraints that necessitate invasive posterior bone grafting. While conventional implant overdentures offer a surgical compromise, they frequently present mechanical complications such as loss of attachment retention and gradual collapse of the vertical dimension of occlusion over the long term. To address these limitations, this clinical report introduces a versatile paradigm utilizing implant-supported surveyed crowns (ISSCs) to retain an implant-assisted removable partial denture (IARPD).Case presentationThis report details the rehabilitation of four completely edentulous patients utilizing this protocol for two distinct purposes. First, it served as a primary rehabilitation strategy to circumvent invasive posterior bone grafting in medically compromised patients. Second, it acted as a prosthodontic revision strategy that repurposed existing, well-integrated fixtures from failing conventional overdentures, resolving severe biological and mechanical complications caused by problematic attachments. By strategically utilizing anterior implants to support splinted ISSCs and a distal extension IARPD, this approach provided stable vertical occlusal support and mitigated destructive cantilever effects. Over a follow-up period of up to 67 months, clinical and radiographic evaluations demonstrated favorable peri-implant tissue health with minimal marginal bone resorption (mean 0.44 ± 0.24mm). Furthermore, mechanical complications were minor and readily manageable, and patients reported a high level of masticatory and esthetic satisfaction.ConclusionsThe ISSC-retained IARPD is a predictable and minimally invasive treatment option for completely edentulous patients. By successfully bridging the biomechanical gap between fixed prostheses and conventional overdentures, it serves as both a primary and revision treatment. The favorable clinical outcomes of this protocol requires strategic implant distribution, precise prosthodontic design, and regular monitoring to prevent biomechanical overload.

papers.title: Comparison of the aesthetic impact on the mandibular angle of two types of osteotomy.
papers.abstract: The growing aesthetic demand for projection and definition of the mandibular angle has challenged oral and maxillofacial surgeons, requiring new approaches to osteotomies during orthognathic surgery. papers.title: Future perspectives of propolis-chitosan biomembranes in wound healing: molecular mechanism, formulation and therapeutic properties.
papers.abstract: Wound management remains a persistent global health burden because conventional dressings largely address the symptoms of a wound rather than the disrupted molecular signalling that stalls its healing. Rather than cataloguing the properties and applications of propolis and chitosan in isolation, this review interrogates the mechanistic basis by which their combination as a biomembrane redirects wound biology. Although attention to propolis-chitosan systems is increasing, the physicochemical basis of their interaction remains poorly understood. Specifically, how chitosan's cationic amine groups interact with propolis polyphenols via hydrogen bonding, electrostatic forces, and possible covalent crosslinking is unclear. Consequently, structure-property relationships affecting membrane crosslinking, swelling, degradation, and controlled release remain unresolved. Chitosan supplies a structural scaffold that supports cellular adhesion and migration, while propolis provides flavonoids and caffeic acid phenethyl ester (CAPE), which engage defined molecular targets across the repair cascade. We reconstruct this cascade stepwise, starting with hemostasis: chitosan-mediated platelet and erythrocyte interactions, leading to clot formation; inflammation: suppression of NF-κB and MAPK to resolve excessive inflammatory signaling; proliferation: early re-epithelialization through H2O2 and AQP3 activation; proliferation: fibroblast activation and granulation tissue formation through TGF-β/Smad signaling; proliferation: angiogenesis and vascular recruitment through PI3K/eNOS/NO and VEGF; and remodeling: collagen-I deposition, fibroblast maturation, and extracellular matrix organization. By linking each formulation property to the specific signalling axis it modulates, rather than treating bioactivity and application as separate narratives, this review identifies where mechanistic evidence is strongest and where critical gaps persist, particularly around dose-dependent pathway crosstalk, batch-to-batch propolis variability, and the translation of ex vivo mechanistic findings into standardized, scalable membranes. Chitosan-propolis nanocomposite biomembranes meet the core requirements of an effective wound dressing (mechanical strength, selective permeability, biodegradability, and biocompatibility), and emerging imaging and molecular tools now make it possible to directly interrogate these signalling pathways within the biomaterial rather than inferring them by analogy. By integrating formulation science with an explicit molecular-mechanism framework, this review positions propolis-chitosan biomembranes as a mechanistically grounded, clinically translatable platform for next-generation wound-care strategies.

papers.title: Phasic metabolic remodeling coordinates cardiac myofibroblast differentiation and function.
papers.abstract: Fibroblast differentiation into matrix-producing, contractile myofibroblasts is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but whether these changes precede differentiation or arise from the activated phenotype remains unclear. We integrated time-resolved extracellular flux analysis, transcriptomics, stable isotope-resolved metabolomics, and metabolic interventions to define the relationship between metabolism and myofibroblast differentiation in adult mouse cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ). TGFβ increased glycolysis within 1.5 h, before broad transcriptional remodeling and induction of periostin and α-smooth muscle actin. Mitochondrial respiration initially declined but increased at 48 h as the phenotype emerged, accompanied by smaller, less elongated mitochondria and greater respiratory capacity. [U-13C6]-glucose tracing revealed progressive incorporation of glucose-derived carbon into glycolytic intermediates, nucleotide sugars, and glycerol 3-phosphate, followed later by increased labeling of tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates. TGFβ-treated fibroblasts also demonstrated enhanced insulin-stimulated glycolysis. Replacing glucose with galactose attenuated collagen and periostin induction, whereas glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase inhibition prevented induction of collagen, periostin, and α-smooth muscle actin. Conversely, glucose transporter 1 or mutant PFK2 (GlycoHi) overexpression increased glycolysis without inducing myofibroblast markers. Together, these loss- and gain-of-function studies indicate that glycolytic activity is required for complete differentiation but is not sufficient to initiate the phenotype. Inhibition of mitochondrial Complex I or ATP synthase preferentially reduced collagen abundance, while glycolytic and Complex I inhibition diminished TGFβ-induced collagen gel contraction. These findings define a phasic metabolic program in which early glycolytic activation precedes transcriptional and phenotypic remodeling, whereas mitochondrial respiratory capacity increases later and distinct metabolic nodes selectively regulate collagen abundance and contractile behavior.

papers.title: Single-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages. We further highlight cohort biases, reproducibility challenges, dissociation artifacts, computational ambiguity, and privacy concerns that constrain immediate clinical implementation. Together, these advances position single-cell profiling as a mechanistic discovery platform with substantial translational promise, contingent on standardization, validation across diverse cohorts, and integration with functional perturbation approaches.

papers.title: Spatial Neighborhood Construction and NICHES Connectomics for Differential Ligand-Receptor Analysis in Fibrotic Human Lung.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables measurement of gene expression within intact tissue architecture, yet most analytical workflows emphasize cell-type classification over cellular interaction. The workflow defines spatial neighborhoods and constructs a directed connectomics graph in which edges represent the set of inferred LR interactions between cells. A parallel Neighborhood Composition assay characterizes the local tissue architecture of the spatial neighborhoods. The framework is modular and tunable: users may adjust neighborhood definitions, select alternative LR databases, and modify scoring and aggregation methods. These node- and edge-aligned data layers support visualization, clustering, and differential analysis of spatially organized signaling patterns. Applied to fibrotic lung tissue, the workflow segregates architecturally defined neighborhoods and identifies differential LR mechanisms that distinguish fibrotic regions from surrounding tissue. This protocol provides a reproducible framework for studying spatially organized intercellular communication across tissues and disease contexts.

papers.title: Manufacturing Route-Dependent Biointerface Modulation in 3D-Printed and Conventional Dental Implant Systems.

papers.title: 'Syphilis is a normal thing that children are born with..' Understanding Barriers and Facilitators to Maternal and Congenital Syphilis Care in Kampala, Uganda
papers.abstract: IntroductionCongenital syphilis (CS) remains a major cause of preventable stillbirths and neonatal deaths globally. ResultsParticipants valued syphilis screening and treatment to protect infant health, particularly when they understood the consequences of untreated infection. Facilitators included respectful counselling, phone-based follow-up, and integration of testing into routine antenatal care. Key barriers included fear of painful injections, stigma and disclosure risk, low male-partner involvement, fragmented information systems, limited infant diagnostics, and medication stockouts. Partner notification was hindered by fears of infidelity accusations and relationship conflict. Notably, caregivers frequently refused treatment for asymptomatic infants due to misconceptions that only visibly ill children required care. Facility opportunities to strengthen the syphilis care cascade were identified such patient tracing systems and strengthened supply chains. Stronger supply chains, integrated maternal-infant-partner care pathways, better-equipped health workers, male-engagement strategies, and consistent follow-up are needed to accelerate elimination of mother-to-child syphilis transmission in Uganda and similar settings. Barriers included fear of injections, stigma, low male-partner involvement, weak information systems, stockouts of supplies, lack of CS confirmatory tests and caregivers refusing prolonged intravenous treatment for infants without symptoms. papers.title: Exhaustive white blood cell extraction and profiling across whole-slide images of blood and bone marrow smears
papers.abstract: Blood and bone marrow smears are central to diagnosing hematological disorders. papers.title: Probabilistic uncertainty in virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology is largely redundant with the predicted mean
papers.abstract: Deep learning has enabled virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology, offering a scalable approach to molecular profiling of routinely archived tissue without molecular assays. However, reliable uncertainty estimates are essential for identifying potentially inaccurate predictions, and it remains unclear whether existing methods provide useful information about prediction reliability. Here, we present a systematic benchmark of uncertainty estimation for virtual spatial transcriptomics across three cancer cohorts spanning melanoma, lung, and kidney tumors. We evaluate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty using probabilistic likelihoods and approximate Bayesian methods alongside histology-free and training-free baselines, assessing both calibration and error informativeness. Across cohorts and methods, uncertainty is associated with prediction error, but the predicted mean largely explains this association. After accounting for the mean, uncertainty provides only weak information about larger errors. Moreover, good calibration does not imply informative uncertainty, with simple distributions fitted without histology achieving comparable calibration. We therefore distinguish calibrated from informative uncertainty and argue that uncertainty should provide information about prediction error beyond the predicted mean. papers.title: Navigating the rapidly evolving landscape of sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics technologies: a comprehensive multi-platform benchmark
papers.abstract: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics assays offer exciting opportunities to profile transcriptome-wide expression with multicellular to even subcellular spatial resolution. papers.title: Biological and technical spatial variation in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies enable the identification of spatially variable genes that can shed light on tissue structure and function. papers.title: Urinary Biomarkers in Cancer: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains a major global health challenge and a leading cause of mortality worldwide. As incidence continues to rise, early detection remains one of the most effective strategies for improving survival and reducing disease burden. Urine is an attractive source of biomarkers due to its non-invasive collection, ease of repeated sampling, and rich molecular composition. Promising diagnostic accuracy was reported for multiple biomarker classes, particularly multimarker panels integrating metabolites, proteins, nucleic acids, and epigenetic signatures. However, most studies were exploratory, involving small cohorts, methodological heterogeneity, and limited independent validation. Urinary biomarkers represent a promising and rapidly evolving approach to non-invasive cancer detection. Despite encouraging diagnostic performance, few candidates have progressed to clinical implementation. Large prospective multicentre studies, rigorous validation, and assay standardisation are essential to establish urinary biomarkers as reliable tools for cancer screening, early diagnosis, and risk stratification.

papers.title: Cancer Cell Metabolic Reprogramming: Dietary, Pharmacological Strategies and Clinical Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming, a key feature of cancer progression that enables tumor adaptation to stress and therapy, represents an emerging target in anticancer research through dietary and pharmacological modulation. papers.title: Case Report: Favorable long-term outcomes of autologous PRF-augmented delayed replantation for traumatic avulsion of three mandibular anterior teeth with 10-year follow-up.
papers.abstract: The first-line treatment for permanent tooth avulsion is immediate replantation. Delayed replantation is associated with a high risk of survival-related complications, such as root resorption. Autologous platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) may promote the periodontal healing of delayed-replanted avulsed teeth and may potentially reduce the occurrence and progression of early root resorption. This case report explores the dental treatment process of autologous PRF-assisted delayed replantation in an adult patient with the avulsion of three mandibular anterior teeth. After an accident, the patient wiped the roots of the avulsed teeth and stored them in dry tissue. Two hours later, the patient visited the emergency department for treatment. On the same day, PRF granules were prepared, and the teeth were replanted with the granules and fixed with semi-elastic splints. The treatment was based on the 2012 guidelines of the International Association of Dental Traumatology. Two weeks later, the patient returned, and root canal treatment was performed, the fixation device was removed at the same visit. Two weeks after intracanal medication with calcium hydroxide, root canal filling was completed. Follow-up visits at 3, 6, and 12 months and up to 10 years after the trauma revealed no clinical symptoms in the affected teeth, and radiography showed no sign of root resorption. The patient expressed satisfaction with both the esthetic and functional outcomes. This case report describes a favorable outcome following PRF-assisted replantation of delayed-replanted avulsed teeth. The findings suggest a potential adjunctive role of PRF in promoting periodontal healing, which warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Bilayer Polycaprolactone (Mitomycin C)/Poly(L-Lactic Acid)/Gelatine (Dimethyloxalylglycine) Nanofibres for Diabetic Wound Repair.
papers.abstract: Background: Diabetic skin wounds arise from chronic hyperglycaemia, peripheral neuropathy, microvascular dysfunction, and compromised immunity. Chronic ulcers are further complicated by infection and local ischaemia-hypoxia, which collectively impede tissue repair. Conventional interventions, including glycaemic control, anti-infective therapy, debridement, and wound dressings, can only partially relieve clinical symptoms. Since these strategies fail to reverse ischaemia-hypoxia or restore the reparative capacity of endogenous cells, ulcers often recur, healing outcomes remain unsatisfactory, and limb amputation may become unavoidable. To overcome these drawbacks, we fabricated a bilayer electrospun microfibre membrane for diabetic wound repair. Methods: An electrospun microfibre membrane with a bilayer structure was fabricated. The outer layer, composed of polycaprolactone (PCL), provided mechanical support and enabled sustained release of mitomycin C (MMC). The inner layer, formulated with a 7:3 ratio of poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) to gelatine (Gel), was designed to match the mechanical properties of the wound bed and was loaded with dimethyloxalylglycine (DMOG). Antibacterial assays against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, as well as proangiogenic evaluations in ischaemic tissues, were conducted to characterise this composite membrane. Results: The outer PCL layer provided mechanical support and enabled sustained MMC release, producing effective antibacterial effects against E. coli and S. aureus. The DMOG-incorporated inner PLLA/GEL layer displayed favourable mechanical compatibility with wound tissue and successfully promoted angiogenesis under ischaemic conditions. By remodelling the wound microenvironment, the biomaterial improved vascularisation and decreased the bacterial load, ultimately accelerating the repair of diabetic skin wounds. Conclusions: This bilayer electrospun membrane integrates antibacterial and pro-angiogenic functions, showing promising application potential for the treatment of diabetic skin wounds.

papers.title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Infection-Associated Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition: Implication in Tumorigenesis and Pathogenesis of HPV-Positive Cancers.
papers.abstract: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a programmed and reversible process that allows epithelial cells to temporarily acquire a mesenchymal cell phenotype with increased migratory and invasive capacity. Analogous phenotypic modulation can also occur in carcinoma cells, which, after undergoing EMT, exhibit cancer stem cell-like properties and actively migrate, leading to tumor invasion and metastases. This structured narrative review focuses on the molecular crosstalk between human papillomavirus (HPV) and EMT, which occurs in HPV-infected human epithelium and in HPV-positive cancers of different location (cervical, head and neck, colorectal, lung, and others). The main questions addressed here are: (i) how HPV-driven EMT may contribute to the malignant transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells, (ii) what mechanistic links may exist between the HPV positivity and EMT in human cancers, and (iii) how EMT in various HPV-positive human tumors may influence their pathogenesis, treatment modalities and outcomes. The relationship between HPV infection and EMT program is delineated as a complex multicomponent mechanism triggered by exogenous and endogenous stimuli and involving specific ligand-receptor interactions, membrane channels, transcription factors, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulators, etc. The review also discusses some of the potential applications of EMT-related biomarkers and molecular targets in the prevention, prediction and treatment of HPV-induced cancers.

papers.title: Hallmarks of aging in systemic sclerosis: implications for pathogenesis, multimorbidity, and therapeutic development.
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease characterised by marked clinical variability and a substantial burden of comorbidities, which may reflect underlying biological aging processes. Although chronological age influences disease presentation and prognosis, growing evidence suggests that biological aging processes may contribute directly to disease pathogenesis. Hallmarks of aging, including chronic low-grade inflammation and immunosenescence, have been identified across tissues affected by SSc and may drive persistent immune activation, vascular injury, defective tissue repair, and progressive fibrosis. Aging is increasingly recognised as a tissue-specific and multidimensional process rather than a uniform consequence of chronological time. Differential aging trajectories across organs may influence susceptibility to SSc-related damage, shaping heterogeneous clinical phenotypes. Aging-related mechanisms may also affect disease presentation, severity, comorbidities, and outcomes across the life course and contribute to therapeutic challenges in routine care. In this review, we examine current evidences linking molecular and cellular mechanism of aging to the pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and outcomes of SSc. We discuss the implications for comorbidity burden and treatment decision-making. A deeper understanding of aging-related mechanisms may provide a unifying framework for disease heterogeneity and support the development of more individualised management strategies and therapeutic approaches in SSc.

papers.title: Proteomics and network biology insights into inflammation suppression during prolonged high-altitude hypoxia acclimatization.
papers.abstract: For decades, the study of high-altitude acclimatization has been a vital area of scientific inquiry aimed at enhancing human resilience, particularly in the context of military deployments. Additionally, LXR/RXR and NO signaling pathways may contribute to prolonged high-altitude acclimatization through their roles in lipid metabolism regulation and anti-inflammatory responses. To corroborate the proteomic and pathway-based predictions, ELISA-based quantification of selected inflammatory mediators was performed following prolonged hypoxia exposure. These findings suggest that prolonged exposure to hypoxia may modulate inflammatory responses during acclimatization. Collectively, this study provides new insights into the molecular processes that may facilitate the regulation of inflammation during long-term high-altitude hypoxic acclimatization.

papers.title: Ancient somatosensory circuit architectures employ flexible molecular strategies.
papers.abstract: The extent to which conserved neural circuit architectures depend on shared molecular specification programs remains unclear. Here, we address this question by examining the somatosensory system of the little skate, Leucoraja erinacea, an early-diverging vertebrate that retains ancestral features of both finned and limb-based body plans. Conversely, the combination treatment did not yield satisfactory results for vitiligo in the acral region.

papers.title: Use of a Polylactic Acid Membrane for Wound Care After Severe Herpes Zoster (Shingles): A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Herpes zoster (HZ) results from reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus and disproportionately affects older adults. Antiviral therapy and systemic analgesia are well established, but local wound care of the eroded skin remains largely empirical: no dressing has been validated in controlled trials for this indication, and denuded HZ lesions are frequently mismanaged with dry gauze that adheres to the wound bed and aggravates pain. Case Presentation: An 85-year-old man with no known chronic disease presented with a one-week history of thoracic HZ unresponsive to outpatient antiviral therapy, requiring admission for uncontrolled pain (9/10 on the Numeric Rating Scale, NRS), vomiting, asthenia, and hyporexia. Examination revealed confluent, superficial-partial-thickness erosions across the T6-T8 dermatomes (12.5 × 24 cm). After a negative wound culture, a single polylactic-acid-based membrane (Suprathel®250) was applied over the entire denuded area. Pain decreased from 9/10 to 2/10 on the NRS within seven days and complete re-epithelialization was observed by day 12, under concurrent antiviral and systemic analgesic therapy and the patient resumed independent daily activities by the third week without scarring. Conclusions: In this single uncontrolled case, pain reduction and wound closure followed one application of a polylactic acid membrane to an extensive HZ lesion. Because antiviral and analgesic therapy were given concurrently and HZ improves spontaneously over time, no causal or comparative inference is possible; the observation is hypothesis-generating and supports further controlled investigation. Suprathel® is CE-marked and FDA-cleared for burn and wound care, so its use for HZ erosions extends an established burn indication.

papers.title: Systemic sclerosis markedly impairs health-related quality of life: a single-centre tertiary cohort study with literature-based comparison to leading causes of global disease burden.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSystemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune condition that significantly impacts the physical and mental health of affected individuals, disrupting their daily life and overall well-being. However, its impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has not been thoroughly compared to other chronic diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and stroke, the impact of which is clearly established. We explored how SSc influences HRQoL and compared its effect to that of six chronic diseases, considered the global leading causes of disease burden in high-income countries, and three common rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases.MethodsWe collected HRQoL data from SSc patients enrolled in a cross-sectional observational study at The Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust, UK. We used the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 to measure HRQoL and compared the participants' scores to published data on unipolar major depression, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, lung cancer, osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain. Mean norm-based transformed scores (NBS) were compared for all eight SF-36 health domains.ResultsThe 121 SSc patients (106 female; mean age = 57 years, standard deviation = 12.3), disease duration mean = 9.50 years, standard deviation = 7.4) in our study reported significantly worse perceived general health (mean (x̄) NBS = 32.82) than the other nine diseases reported in the literature. Role limitations due to physical problems (x̄ NBS = 34.77) were comparable to stroke, RA, and lung cancer. Significant impairments were noted in bodily pain (x̄ NBS = 36), similar to osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain, as well as vitality (x̄ NBS = 39.69), comparable to RA. Emotional role limitations (x̄ NBS = 41.78) were second only to major depression, similar to stroke and RA.ConclusionsWe found that SSc has a substantial impact on HRQoL, resulting in significant physical and psychological impairment comparable to that experienced by patients with RA and stroke. These findings contextualise the burden of SSc and may inform future research and clinical practice aimed at improving patient care.

papers.title: Tocilizumab in refractory pretibial myxedema: new therapeutic insights.

papers.abstract: BackgroundAntibody-mediated rejection (AMR) of liver allografts remains incompletely defined, particularly in biopsies classified as indeterminate for AMR under the current Banff criteria. papers.title: The sirtuin family: from mechanisms to therapy.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRT1-SIRT7) are evolutionarily conserved NAD+-dependent deacylases that function as metabolic sensors, coupling cellular metabolic state to epigenetic, transcriptional and post-translational regulatory programs across distinct subcellular compartments. Despite two decades of research, isoform- and disease-specific aspects remain poorly integrated, limiting both conceptual clarity and therapeutic translation. This review synthesizes recent advances in sirtuin biology into a family-wide framework. Rather than functioning as isolated longevity factors, sirtuins operate as a distributed compartmentalized regulatory network in which nuclear SIRT1, SIRT6 and SIRT7, cytosolic SIRT2 and mitochondrial SIRT3, SIRT4 and SIRT5 collectively govern glucose and lipid metabolism, mitochondrial quality control, autophagy, inflammation and immune tolerance. This network operates across metabolic disorders, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer, where dysregulated sirtuin signalling influences disease development in a disease- and tissue-specific manner. Therapeutic strategies are evaluated, ranging from isoform-selective small-molecule modulators and NAD+-targeted interventions to emerging protein-degradation approaches, with isoform selectivity, off-target effects and the systemic consequences of NAD+ modulation identified as key translational barriers that have contributed to heterogeneous clinical outcomes. Viewing sirtuins as a context-sensitive compartmentalized network, not isolated targets, offers a coherent framework to guide mechanistic interrogation and the design of more precise sirtuin-based therapies, with priority areas including tissue-selective degradation and network-level biomarkers.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms in health and disease.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms, serving as a crucial temporal bridge linking neural activity and pathological biology, are regulated by central pacemaker neurons to maintain cellular homeostasis and coordinate diverse biological processes. Circadian rhythm disruption is closely associated with various diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Circadian rhythms are controlled by core clock genes, such as BMAL1 and CLOCK, modulating numerous physiological processes, encompassing metabolism, immune responses, neural activity, and hormone regulation. Circadian rhythms disruptions arising from shift work, jet lag, or inconsistent sleep schedules are implicated in both the onset and progression of numerous diseases, notably Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The article highlights how circadian dysregulation alters cellular processes to potentially accelerate disease progression. Circadian disruption results in impaired immune function, further promoting disease development and resistance to treatment. Potential therapeutic applications based on circadian biology, such as chronotherapy and personalized medicine, are also discussed. Recent technological advances, embodied in wearable devices and omics approaches, are increasingly providing deeper insights into circadian biology. Further unveiling the role of circadian in health and disease opens new avenues for tailoring treatment timing to patients' biological rhythms, thereby enhancing therapeutic outcomes across various diseases. By bridging fundamental circadian mechanisms with clinical pathology, this review provides a roadmap for future chronotherapeutic interventions in precision medicine.

papers.title: Janus-structured piezoelectric membrane couples barrier protection with pathological microenvironment-responsive bioactivity for periodontal bone regeneration.
papers.abstract: Periodontal bone regeneration remains challenging due to the persistent infection-inflammation-bone resorption cycle and the rapid invasion of epithelial and gingival connective tissues into defect sites. A dense PLLA layer facing soft tissues prevents premature tissue infiltration and maintains regenerative space, while a porous defect-facing interface functionalized with ZnO nanowires provides bioactive regulation. The ZnO nanowires enhance the overall piezoelectric response of the membrane and enable pH-responsive Zn2+ release under the acidic periodontal microenvironment, thereby delivering antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic cues. One week after implantation, peripheral neutrophil percentage decreased to approximately 21% of those in the J-PLLA group, accompanied by reduced tumor necrosis factor-α expression and increased cluster of differentiation 206 expression, consistent with a shift toward a reparative macrophage phenotype. At week 6, J-PLLA-ZnO increased the osteocalcin-positive bone-forming area by approximately 1.5-fold compared with non-Janus PLLA-ZnO, indicating improved periodontal bone regeneration. Moreover, the cementoenamel junction-alveolar bone crest distance was reduced by approximately 40% relative to untreated controls. Meanwhile, the membrane underwent gradual biodegradation throughout the healing process. These findings demonstrate that integrating spatial barrier function with pH-responsive bioactivity represents a promising strategy for guided tissue regeneration in inflammatory periodontal defects.

papers.title: Recent advances in protein extraction methods from bone tissue for proteomics analysis.

papers.title: Multiscale heterostructured Mg-2 Zn alloy for biodegradable implants: Coordinated strength-ductility, moderate degradation, and immunomodulation.
papers.abstract: High-strength lean-alloy magnesium (Mg) has attracted extensive attention for orthopedic and vascular stent implants owing to its favorable biodegradability and biocompatibility. However, while retaining the chemical composition of specimens and ensuring high biosafety, the major challenge is to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off and achieve uniform degradation behavior. The alloy possessed a bimodal heterogeneous structure composed of fine-grained regions containing nanograins and nanotwins, as well as coarse-grained regions. It attained an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 350 MPa with an elongation of 13%. This heterostructured Mg-2Zn alloy exhibits better performance compared with the commercial rare-earth-containing WE43 alloy. Moreover, it demonstrated slow degradation rates (0.07 mm·year-1 in vitro and 0.11 mm·year-1 in vivo) driven by multi-phase interface effects. Furthermore, the heterostructured Mg-2 Zn alloy exhibited antibacterial activity in vitro and a relatively mild peri‑implant inflammatory response in vivo. This study differs from conventional rare-earth alloy strengthening strategies, clarifies the formation and regulation mechanisms of heterostructures, and provides theoretical and technical support for the clinical translation of high-performance biodegradable Mg alloys. papers.title: Microneedle-based drug delivery for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases: current applications and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases encompass a spectrum of conditions that arise from dysregulated immune-inflammatory responses marked by a chronic clinical course, a propensity for relapse, and a tendency to cause significant ocular tissue damage, which can lead to profound impairment of visual function. Dysregulation of the balance between immune cell subpopulations is central to the pathogenesis of many of these diseases. At present, non-specific treatments such as glucocorticoids and immunosuppressants form the cornerstone of therapy for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases. However, these treatments often suffer from poor bioavailability and targeting, cumbersome or invasive administration methods, and are associated with side effects such as increased intraocular pressure (IOP), cataracts, or glaucoma with frequent administration. These limitations underscore the urgent need for alternative drug delivery methods. Microneedles have emerged as an innovative approach to ocular drug delivery, offering distinct advantages over traditional eye drops and intravitreal injections. They enhance drug penetration and targeting, provide sustained release, and may reduce unnecessary drug exposure, thus holding great promise for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases. This review aims to shed light on the unique benefits and efficacy of microneedles as drug-delivery systems for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases, with particular attention to noninfectious uveitis, corneal inflammatory disorders, inflammation-associated corneal neovascularization, and allergic conjunctivitis. It also discusses ocular safety and toxicity, manufacturing and standardization, regulatory challenges, and future prospects of microneedle applications, providing a comprehensive overview of their potential for ocular drug delivery.

papers.title: Epigenetic Regulatory Networks in Cardiac Fibrosis: Therapeutic Targets, Crosstalk, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis is a central driver of pathological cardiac remodeling and a critical risk factor for the progression to heart failure. papers.abstract: Aberrant extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling in tumors is characterized by altered deposition, enzymatic cross-linking, degradation, and organization of matrix molecules that in turn can contribute directly to tumor invasiveness, immune evasion, and resistance to therapy. papers.title: Topical MSC-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Accelerate Healing of Second-Degree Burns: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Burn injuries are challenging to treat due to wound progression and long-term scarring. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) have regenerative and immunomodulatory properties that may mitigate these complications. In this phase 1/2a, first-in-human, open-label study, a 48-year-old man with deep second-degree burns received a single topical dose of allogeneic bone marrow MSC-derived EVs within 48 h of injury. The treated wound achieved > 99% closure within 1 week, with durable healing for over 1 year. Scar outcomes improved over 52 weeks, with Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale scores indicating early resolution of pain and pruritus and minimal residual scarring. No adverse events occurred. Laser Doppler imaging showed improved perfusion within 1 week, suggesting prevention of burn wound conversion. These findings support the potential of MSC-derived EVs to accelerate burn healing and reduce scar-related morbidity.
